jobs.excerpt: VetsEZ is currently looking for a VistA/MUMPS Developer for a 100% remote position supporting a large federal government healthcare modernization project.
jobs.description:
VetsEZ is currently looking for a VistA/MUMPS Developer for a 100% remote position supporting a large federal government healthcare modernization project. This role will support a Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) initiative focused on reducing and ultimately eliminating the use of Social Security Numbers (SSNs) within critical VistA applications, workflows, reports, audit records, and related processes. The developer will analyze existing VistA functionality, implement MUMPS/M software modifications, troubleshoot defects, and support the transition from SSN-based processes toward approved enterprise identifiers while reducing exposure of sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII).

This position will work within a remote, multidisciplinary Agile development team alongside Lead VistA Developers, Business Analysts, Product Owners, Quality Assurance personnel, cybersecurity teams, and Government stakeholders. Development activities will support multiple VistA packages, including Admission, Discharge, Transfer (ADT), Patient Care Encounter (PCE), Automated Information Collection System (AICS), Record Tracking, and VistA Audit Solutions.

The candidate must reside within the continental US.

Responsibilities:

  • Modify and enhance VistA/MUMPS applications to eliminate or replace SSN usage within business processes, user interfaces, reports, audit trails, and related functionality while implementing approved approaches for transitioning to enterprise identifiers.
  • Analyze existing VistA routines, data structures, workflows, and application dependencies to identify affected functionality, troubleshoot defects, and implement secure, maintainable code consistent with VA and project development standards.
  • Develop and execute unit tests and support functional, integration, regression, User Acceptance Testing, deployment validation, and production-readiness activities to ensure modifications preserve existing functionality and meet approved requirements.
  • Collaborate with Quality Assurance personnel to investigate defects, implement corrections, verify resolutions, and support post-release troubleshooting and application stability.
  • Follow secure software development and sensitive-data-handling practices when working with PII and PHI, support applicable VA privacy, security, and NIST control requirements, and produce technical documentation describing application changes and implementation considerations.
  • Collaborate with Lead Developers, Business Analysts, Product Owners, QA personnel, cybersecurity teams, and other stakeholders within an Agile environment, participating in Sprint Planning, backlog refinement, daily stand-ups, Sprint Reviews, and Retrospectives while communicating estimates, technical issues, dependencies, and risks.
  • Take on additional tasks and responsibilities as needed to support team objectives and ensure the success of the project.

Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience, with 5+ years of professional VistA/MUMPS development experience.
  • Strong hands-on experience programming within VistA using MUMPS/M and InterSystems Caché, GT.M, or a comparable M-based platform.
  • Experience modifying or supporting VistA packages, modules, data structures, or other healthcare information systems, including analysis of existing routines, workflows, and application dependencies.
  • Experience with software debugging and troubleshooting, source control, peer code review, unit and integration testing, and Agile software development practices.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with an understanding of secure software development practices and the ability to accurately troubleshoot complex application issues.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively within a multidisciplinary software development team and communicate technical issues, dependencies, and risks.

Additional Qualifications:

Ready to help shape how innovative medicines reach patients and healthcare providers across the healthcare ecosystem? As the Associate Director, Market Access Contracting, you will play a critical role in developing and managing market access agreements across Managed Care, Medi-care, Advanced Platforms, and Channel contracts. Provide general oversight to discount and rebate operations team and serve as an approver of various contract price determinations and payment types related to market access contracts (e.g., Managed Care and Medicare rebate payments, GPO, channel, and customer contract price and rebate payments).

Reporting will include but not limited to formulary tracking, rate tracking, invoice tracking, growth and performance-based rebate tracking across customers and/or channel segments, and general reporting of market share using both claims, IQVIA, sales, and chargeback data.

  • Engage on an ongoing basis with MMF Gross to Net forecasting team to review contract changes, actual blended rates forecasted blended rates, and associated P&L implications for each account.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to present complex information and data sets in an understandable and compelling manner.

The Association of periOperative Registered Nurses (AORN) is seeking a Sr Manager, Segment Marketing – Nursing and Consumer Products to help advance patient and staff safety through evidence-based practice, education, and clinical resources that support perioperative nurses. jobs.title: Customer Growth Marketing Manager - North America
jobs.excerpt: About ZensaiZensai is the Human Success company.  Our agentic AI platform coaches employees and managers through learning, performance, and engagement, natively inside Microsoft 365.
jobs.description:
About Zensai

Zensai is the Human Success company. Our agentic AI platform coaches employees and managers through learning, performance, and engagement, natively inside Microsoft 365. More than 2,000 organizations use Zensai to make development part of how work happens, rather than a separate HR destination.

We believe the more AI we have, the more human we need to be. This role is where that belief meets our customers.

Why this role exists

Our biggest growth opportunity sits with the customers we already have. Over the next few years we plan to grow 3.6x from our existing customer base — and that growth depends on customers who stay, adopt more, and move up our editions.

You are Marketing's person in North America for that customer base. You know our customers in the region better than anyone in Marketing: who they are, what they're trying to achieve, where they're thriving, and where they're at risk. You turn that understanding into programs that keep customers engaged, grow accounts, and surface the stories that help us win more.

This is a marketing role that shows up with Sales. Under our go-to-market model, each region runs as a cross-functional pod — AEs, AMs, CSMs, solution and GTM engineers, and marketing — aligned around the customer. You're a member of the North America pod: in customer meetings, in sales meetings, and in the room when regional priorities are set. You know the region's objectives as well as the people carrying the number.

This is a generalist customer marketing role with a commercial number attached. You'll work hand in hand with Customer Success and Account Managers in the region, alongside our Lifecycle Marketing Manager and the central marketing team.

Where you sit

Solid line - Marketing — priorities, standards, brand and messaging, performance review, career development

Dotted line - RVP Sales, North America — regional revenue priorities, target accounts, program focus

Closest partners - Customer Success Managers and Account Managers in North America · Lifecycle Marketing Manager · Product Marketing · Brand & Content · GTM Engineering

Counterpart - Customer Growth Marketing Manager, EMEA — one shared playbook, two regions

Regional pod - AEs, AMs, CSMs, SE/GTM Engineer, BDR, Channel in North America

Cadence you join - Weekly working session with the RVP · weekly pipeline review and forecast call · weekly account and renewal review with CS and AMs · customer and sales meetings · monthly regional business review · quarterly planning with central marketing

Where regional and central priorities conflict, Marketing leadership and the RVP resolve it together. You flag early rather than absorb the trade-off.

What you own

  • The regional customer strategy — the North America customer marketing plan, set with the RVP and regional commercial leadership.

  • Expansion pipeline and ARR influenced by your programs in North America.

  • Retention contribution — at-risk accounts reached and re-engaged before renewal.

  • Customer stories — a steady supply of case studies, references, reviews, and speakers from the region.

  • Program performance — what worked, what didn't, and what we do next, reported monthly.

What you'll do

Set the regional strategy

  • Own the plan: set the North America customer marketing strategy in partnership with the RVP, regional sales, and commercial leadership — which customers, which industries, which programs, and what each should deliver.

  • Tie it to the number: build the plan from the region's revenue, renewal, and expansion objectives, and revisit it every quarter.

  • Report back: bring program-sourced pipeline, expansion ARR influenced, and retention results into each regional business review.

Show up with Sales

  • In the meetings: join customer meetings, account planning, pipeline reviews, and forecast calls — so programs are built against live regional priorities, not a central calendar.

  • Run the matrix cadence: hold a standing weekly working session with the RVP to agree priorities, target accounts, and success measures.

  • Be the connector: share engagement and risk signals with AEs, AMs, and CSMs so they know where to act first, and make sure handoffs between marketing and the commercial team are tight.

Know the customer base, deeply

  • Build the regional picture: segment customers by industry, edition, size, adoption, and renewal date — and know which accounts are ready to grow and which are drifting.

  • Understand motivations: what CHROs, HR and L&D leaders, and IT leaders in our customer base care about, and what makes them stay.

  • Bring the customer into the room: share what you learn with Product Marketing, Brand, and Sales so it shapes positioning, content, and roadmap conversations.

Turn signals into programs

  • Risk signals: working with the Lifecycle Marketing Manager and CS, design programs that respond to falling usage, champion changes, low engagement, or upcoming renewals — before they become churn.

  • Growth signals: spot accounts showing expansion intent and build plays with AMs to act on them.

  • Test and refine: agree what each program should move, measure it, and keep what works.

Run industry programs

  • Vertical-first: design industry-specific programs for our key sectors in North America — such as financial services, legal, manufacturing, healthcare, professional services, and retail.

  • Relevant content: work with Brand & Content to build stories, guides, and proof that speak to each industry's real challenges.

Grow accounts

  • Expansion programs: partner with AMs to run edition moves (Grow → Scale → Transform), cross-sell, and adoption programs such as Copilot readiness.

  • Account plays: run targeted programs for high-potential customer accounts, with account lists agreed with the RVP and AMs.

  • Equip the team: design offers, plays, templates, and talk tracks that AEs, AMs, and CSMs can take straight to customers — with consistent messaging across the portfolio and regions, and clear follow-up actions for every program.

Create moments that matter

  • Customer moments in region: user groups, roundtables, executive dinners, webinars, and moments around the major US HR and L&D events — designed to connect customers with each other and with Zensai.

  • Community: work with our Head of Community so regional moments feed the wider Zensai community.

Find and tell the right stories

  • Source the stories: identify customers with outcomes worth sharing and bring them forward for case studies, video, references, reviews, and speaking slots.

  • Build advocates: grow a bench of customers who will speak for Zensai — and look after them.

Work with the central team

  • Central builds, region deploys: use central brand, product marketing, and lifecycle programs, and adapt them for your region rather than starting from scratch.

  • Use AI well: use AI and our signal tools (HubSpot, Dynamics 365, Gong, Dreamdata, Clay) for research, segmentation, and first drafts — and keep the judgment, the stories, and the customer relationships human.

What you'll bring

  • 4+ years in B2B SaaS marketing, ideally in customer, lifecycle, or account-based marketing.

  • Customer-first instinct — you enjoy talking to customers and you're genuinely curious about what drives them.

  • Comfort with numbers — you can read usage, renewal, and pipeline data, find the story in it, and decide what to do.

  • Program builder — you've designed and run multi-touch programs end to end, from idea to results.

  • Commercial partnering — you've worked inside or alongside sales and CS teams, joined customer conversations, and earned their trust.

  • Matrix experience — you can deliver to a commercial leader while holding one marketing standard.

  • Clear communicator — excellent written and spoken English.

  • Tool fluency — confident with HubSpot (preferred) and a CRM such as Dynamics 365 or Salesforce; comfortable using AI tools every day.

  • Self-starter — comfortable owning a region and working across time zones with the central team.

Benefits

Time for Life: We offer employees 25 days of PTO plus 11 federal holidays, and we provide 6 months of paid leave for primary caregivers and 4 months for secondary caregivers.

401(k) that stands out: We match up to 6% from day one. Your future, growing faster.

Health cover that starts day 1: We pay 70% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for you and your family, with two plans plus HSA.

We provide 6 months of paid leave for primary caregivers and 4 months for secondary caregivers.

Learning: 10% of your working time dedicated to development. Built in, not squeezed in.

Peace of mind: Company-paid life insurance (2× salary), disability cover, and AD&D.

Wellbeing perks: Free Headspace family plan, fitness membership (gyms, yoga, apps), and a 24/7 support line with counselling.

jobs.excerpt: DescriptionKeeper Security is hiring a Senior Software Development Engineer in Test (SDET), AI & Automation to join our AI team and help build a modern, automated approach to quality across AI-powered products and services.
jobs.description:
Description

Keeper Security is hiring a Senior Software Development Engineer in Test (SDET), AI & Automation to join our AI team and help build a modern, automated approach to quality across AI-powered products and services. This is a 100% remote position, with an opportunity to work a hybrid schedule for candidates based in the El Dorado Hills, CA or Chicago, IL metro areas.

Keeper’s cybersecurity software is trusted by millions of people and thousands of organizations globally. Keeper is published in 23 languages and sold in over 150 countries. Join one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity companies and help establish scalable quality engineering practices for AI-driven systems operating in security-sensitive environments.

About Keeper

Keeper Security is one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity software companies that protects thousands of organizations and millions of people in over 150 countries. Keeper is a pioneer of zero-knowledge and zero-trust security built for any IT environment. Its core offering, KeeperPAM®, is an AI-enabled, cloud-native platform that protects all users, devices and infrastructure from cyber attacks. Recognized for its innovation in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Privileged Access Management (PAM), Keeper secures passwords and passkeys, infrastructure secrets, remote connections and endpoints with role-based enforcement policies, least privilege and just-in-time access. Learn why Keeper is trusted by leading organizations to defend against modern adversaries at KeeperSecurity.com.

About the Job

As a Senior SDET, AI & Automation, you will serve as an embedded quality engineering partner within Keeper’s AI team. You will work alongside engineers and Product throughout design and development to define test strategy, establish acceptance criteria and build automated coverage as AI-powered capabilities are being developed.

This role requires experience testing both traditional deterministic software systems and non-deterministic AI/ML systems. Traditional application behavior can often be validated against consistent expected outputs, while AI models may produce different but acceptable results across models, prompts and inputs. You will help design testing approaches that account for this variability while still establishing measurable quality, reliability and safety standards. You will build automation frameworks, develop deterministic and probabilistic validation strategies, integrate testing into CI/CD workflows and help Keeper move toward continuous quality engineering rather than end-of-cycle QA.

Responsibilities

  • Partner directly with AI engineers, Software Engineers and Product Managers during design and development to define test strategy, acceptance criteria and automation requirements
  • Design and maintain automated testing frameworks for AI-powered applications, backend services, APIs and supporting software systems
  • Develop testing strategies for both deterministic software behavior and non-deterministic AI/ML outputs
  • Define measurable evaluation criteria, tolerances and quality thresholds for AI model and LLM-driven functionality
  • Build automated regression, integration, API and end-to-end coverage alongside feature development
  • Develop test harnesses and evaluation workflows for prompts, models, agents, tool-calling workflows and AI-integrated applications
  • Validate AI behavior across different models, prompts, inputs and system configurations
  • Develop automated test utilities using languages such as Python, Java, JavaScript/TypeScript, Rust or similar technologies
  • Integrate automated validation and quality gates into CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI or similar platforms
  • Build and maintain test datasets, mocks, fixtures and synthetic data required for repeatable AI and software validation
  • Analyze model and application failures to distinguish defects, expected model variability, data issues and test instability
  • Evaluate AI outputs for reliability, consistency, safety and alignment with expected product behavior
  • Work with engineering teams to improve application testability, observability and diagnostic capabilities
  • Track test cases, execution results and coverage using TestRail or similar test management platforms
  • Analyze logs, telemetry and system behavior to identify root causes and produce clear, reproducible defect reports
  • Reduce flaky tests and improve the speed, stability and maintainability of automated test suites
  • Contribute to quality engineering standards, AI testing methodologies and automation best practices across Keeper’s AI organization
  • Use AI-assisted tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot or similar platforms to improve automation development, test generation, debugging, analysis and documentation

Requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in SDET, software development, test automation or another code-intensive quality engineering role
  • Hands-on experience testing AI/ML, LLM-powered or model-integrated software systems
  • Strong understanding of the differences between deterministic software testing and non-deterministic AI/ML validation
  • Experience defining evaluation criteria, expected behaviors, tolerances or scoring approaches for AI-driven functionality
  • Strong programming skills in Python, Java, JavaScript/TypeScript, Rust or another general-purpose programming language
  • Significant experience designing, developing and maintaining automated test frameworks
  • Experience building automated functional, integration, API and end-to-end test coverage
  • Experience testing REST APIs and distributed application workflows using tools such as Postman, REST Assured or similar platforms
  • Experience integrating automated tests into CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI or similar technologies
  • Experience working within an Agile software development team with close collaboration between QA, Engineering and Product
  • Strong understanding of shift-left testing, continuous quality and testability principles
  • Experience with TestRail or similar test management platforms
  • Strong debugging and troubleshooting skills using logs, APIs, application telemetry and development tools
  • Experience with Git-based development workflows, code review and modern software engineering practices
  • Familiarity with AI-assisted development and testing tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot or similar technologies
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate variable AI behavior without relying solely on exact-match outcomes
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to collaborate closely with AI engineers, Software Engineers, Product Managers and QA professionals
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience
  • Due to this role’s involvement with FedRAMP compliance requirements, qualified candidates must be a U.S. Person, defined as a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience testing LLMs, agentic systems, retrieval-augmented generation, tool calling or prompt-driven workflows
  • Experience building automated model evaluation, benchmarking or regression frameworks
  • Familiarity with AI evaluation metrics and techniques for measuring quality across non-deterministic outputs
  • Experience with Rust in production or test automation environments
  • Experience with performance, reliability, security or adversarial testing of AI-enabled systems
  • Experience with AI-assisted generation of automated tests or synthetic test data
  • Familiarity with Docker, Kubernetes or cloud-based testing environments
  • Experience testing cybersecurity, identity, PAM or other security-sensitive software
  • Experience building shared automation frameworks or internal testing tools used across engineering teams

Benefits

  • Medical, Dental & Vision (inclusive of domestic partnerships
  • Employer Paid Life Insurance & Employee/Spouse/Child Supplemental life
  • Voluntary Short/Long Term Disability Insurance
  • 401K (Roth/Traditional)
  • A generous PTO plan that celebrates your commitment and seniority (including paid Bereavement/Jury Duty, etc)

The core objective of the role is simple: keep clients happy by ensuring expectations are clearly understood, consistently communicated, and successfully delivered throughout every stage of a job.

The Operations Associate/Coordinator will act as the central connection between clients, third-party vendors, site contacts, and internal teams. They will manage urgent and routine service requests, coordinate vendor visits, drive quoting and documentation, oversee job execution, and ensure every ticket is properly closed with a complete paper trail.

Success in this position requires someone who asks the right questions, keeps track of details, communicates proactively, and follows through relentlessly. The ideal candidate is comfortable handling many active jobs and conversations simultaneously while building strong relationships with both clients and vendors.

Responsibilities
  • Manage maintenance and facilities service requests from initial ticket intake through job completion, invoicing, and closeout.
  • Review incoming client tickets and classify each request according to trade, urgency, scope, and service requirements.
  • Confirm site contacts, access instructions, and relevant job details before vendor dispatch.
  • Identify emergency or highly urgent requests and quickly coordinate with the appropriate dispatch resources.
  • Source qualified third-party vendors primarily through proactive outbound phone calls.
  • Conduct early vendor qualification conversations, including commercial questions related to availability, pricing, scope, and ability to perform the work.
  • Share photos and job information with vendors during calls and verbally confirm that all relevant materials have been received and understood.
  • Schedule and coordinate site visits between vendors and facility contacts.
  • Organize multiple vendor visits efficiently for non-emergency jobs requiring competing bids, including scheduling offset visits on the same day when appropriate.
  • Reconfirm appointments approximately 24 hours in advance to minimize missed visits and delays.
  • Pursue remote estimates whenever possible to accelerate the quoting process.
  • Review, compare, and negotiate vendor quotes, challenging initial estimates when appropriate and balancing cost with turnaround time.
  • Ensure competing bids are based on comparable scopes and clearly document assumptions or differences in writing.
  • Collect and verify required vendor documentation before work is authorized, including W9s, Certificates of Insurance, and signed quotes.
  • Confirm that Certificates of Insurance contain the correct required parties and information.
  • Follow up promptly on missing documentation rather than allowing paperwork gaps to delay job execution.
  • Oversee active work orders by holding vendors accountable to agreed timelines, pricing, and scope.
  • Coordinate site access and resolve logistical issues that could prevent or delay completion.
  • Address scope changes before additional work is performed and obtain the appropriate approvals when required.
  • Maintain proactive communication with clients throughout the job rather than waiting for clients to request updates.
  • Confirm completed work through vendor photos, site confirmation, and other required documentation.
  • Compare completed work and final invoices against the originally approved scope.
  • Route incomplete work or punch-list items back to vendors before considering a job complete.
  • Review, approve, and submit vendor invoices according to established processes.
  • Follow up on client approvals and resolve pricing or billing discrepancies.
  • Close completed jobs in the system with complete documentation and an accurate record of all relevant communications and approvals.

Requirements

  • Previous hands-on experience in a facilities, property maintenance, or service operations environment, with direct exposure to maintenance requests, work orders, vendors, contractors, and/or property-related service coordination.
  • Proven ability to coordinate several active priorities and conversations simultaneously across phone calls, SMS, and email.
  • Comfortable managing approximately 10–30 active communication threads at once, with the organizational skills to prevent important details from being missed.
  • Strong phone communication skills and confidence managing a role where calls are the primary communication channel.
  • Previous experience with cold calling, vendor coordination, operations, dispatch, service coordination, or another phone-intensive position.
  • Demonstrated ability to build professional relationships with both clients and external service providers.
  • Strong negotiation skills and sound judgment when balancing cost, urgency, service quality, and turnaround time.
  • Highly proactive approach to follow-up and problem solving.
  • Excellent organizational skills with the ability to capture, remember, and retrieve important information across multiple active jobs.
  • Strong questioning skills and willingness to gather enough information before making decisions or moving a job forward.
  • Excellent communication habits, including proactive and frequent updates to stakeholders.
  • Strong attention to detail and disciplined documentation practices.
  • Ability to treat required paperwork and pre-work documentation as mandatory rather than optional.
  • Ability to remain composed and effective in a fast-paced, high-volume environment involving urgent requests.
  • Professional-level spoken and written English.

Qualifications
  • Previous experience in a facilities-related role is strongly preferred, such as facilities coordination, property maintenance, field service coordination, maintenance operations, property operations, or vendor/service management.
  • Working knowledge of the facilities service lifecycle, including work-order intake, vendor dispatch, site access, quoting, approvals, service completion, documentation, and invoice closeout.
  • Previous experience usingCMMS or facilities management platforms such as ServiceChannel, MaintainX, or similar systems, with familiarity managing work orders, service requests, vendor activity, and job status updates.
  • Experience working directly with clients, vendors, contractors, maintenance providers, property contacts, or other external service partners.
  • Familiarity with service-ticket and work-order environments is strongly beneficial.
  • Spanish proficiency is a strong plus.
  • Experience supporting U.S.-based clients, facilities, properties, or service operations is advantageous.
  • Comfortable working cross-functionally with operations, dispatch, finance, and vendor-management teams.

Benefits

  • Full-time position
  • 100% remote — work from anywhere in LATAM
  • Opportunity to be part of a growing operations platform with a clear structure and real impact
  • Exposure to a fast-paced, U.S.-based operations model with strong systems and processes
  • Career growth opportunity with potential to move into a supervisory role.

Location: Flexible; home-based (working hours UTC ±3)

CLEAR Global believes in the power of language. Clear communications using the right language will help people live with dignity, act independently, and make their own choices freely. CLEAR Global helps people get vital information and be heard, no matter what language they speak.

CLEAR Global has been at the forefront of the development of inclusive AI for social impact in the Global South for over 10 years, and has built strong partnerships with the Global South AI ecosystem. CLEAR Global plays a role helping to support funders, academic research, local startups, and social impact organizations in driving the use of language AI for social impact, not just for the major languages of power, but more inclusively to reach the more marginalized.

Executive Director Role

The Executive Director of the organization will bring extensive international experience in the social impact sector, particularly focusing on how technology can enable and empower local language speakers. The Executive Director (ED) is responsible for the organization's consistent achievement of its mission and financial objectives.

The ED will help lead the organization to achieve its mission, enabling teams to develop and implement programs, organizational and financial plans. They will work closely with the Board of Directors and with the leadership of CLEAR Global. Within the leadership team, they will envision new strategies and policies authorized by the Board. Given the strong role of volunteers in our work, a priority will be to promote active participation by our community of language enthusiasts.

The successful candidate will be an innovative and inspirational leader with proven skills in motivating grassroots movements, language technology and language AI, fundraising, strategic planning, and an understanding of international nonprofit management. Superior leadership qualifications include expertise in communication, sound financial management, and team and trust building with Board, leadership, staff, and community. This role is about being an inspiring leader.

Responsibilities include:

  • Representing the organization, actively participating in local and global discussions about language technology development and uses, and raising the profile for the organization, its programs, and its goals.
  • Developing and maintaining relationships with key stakeholders, including funders.
  • Superior communication with external stakeholders to galvanize the community and donors to support the movement toward language equity
  • Effective and timely communication with the Board and dissemination of relevant information for the Board to function properly and to make informed decisions.
  • Overseeing the development and maintenance of solid financial planning and meeting financial and operational targets set.
  • Ensuring the integrity and compliance of the organization as per international standards.
  • Developing the strategic direction and leading implementation of CLEAR Global’s mission, bringing clarity, vision, values, and exceptional stewardship for these community resources.
  • Identification of trends and emerging social impact, particularly language technology.
  • Promoting a supportive and positive environment and culture that fosters personal responsibility and commitment to CLEAR Global’s goals and values.
  • Ensuring that CLEAR Global is a safe environment with a living Code of Conduct.
  • Leading by example

Requirements

  • A degree in a related field required; advanced degree preferred.
  • Significant senior-level or executive experience in nonprofits, with at least 10 years of professional leadership experience.
  • Background and experience with the African/Asian language technology ecosystem
  • Demonstrated and effective nonpartisan relationship builder with various constituencies including the Board, the staff, and other organizations
  • A track record of management, operations, fiscal administration; a working knowledge of budgets, finances, strategic planning, and an understanding of international aid
  • Ability to think broadly, critically, strategically, and conceptually with an understanding of how to affect systems change.
  • A professional with high ethical standards of conduct, integrity, and fiduciary duty.
  • Exceptional listening skills, a good sense of humor with humility and a respect for the dignity of those who speak marginalized languages.
  • Familiarity with low-resource languages, inclusive practices and ethical considerations in language data specific to the African continent.
  • Fluent in the English language and preferably a minority language speaker themselves

Organizational Background

CLEAR Global exists to help people get vital information, and be heard, whatever language they speak. We believe that everyone has the right to give and receive information in a language and format they understand. We work with nonprofit partners and a global community of language professionals to build local language translation capacity, and raise awareness of language barriers. Our network of over 100,000 community members translate millions of words of life-saving and life-changing information a year. For more information and to volunteer or donate, please visit: .

Core Values

CLEAR Global employees and volunteers are made of people who believe passionately about the value of this work and take personal responsibility for achieving the mission. CLEAR Global’s mission and organizational spirit are made up of the core values established in its strategic framework:

Excellence: As the leading voice for communicating humanitarian information in the right language, CLEAR Global is a leader in the translation industry and in the non-profit sector.

Integrity: CLEAR Global believes that every person, whether it’s the people who we serve, our volunteers or our staff, has value, deserves respect and has inherent dignity.

Empowerment: CLEAR Global believes in using language to empower people around the world to control their own development and destiny.

Innovation: CLEAR Global recognizes and celebrates the power of innovation to address humanitarian and crisis issues around the world.

Sustainability: CLEAR Global recognizes that meeting our mission necessitates establishment and maintenance of a solid financial and organizational infrastructure.

Tolerance: Our staff and volunteers are highly knowledgeable and skilled; value each other, our partner and our recipients; create a supportive work environment; and, conduct themselves professionally at all times.

CLEAR Global is an equal-opportunity employer, committed to having a diverse team where individuals of all backgrounds collaborate and learn from one another. We believe we can be most effective with diverse experience and expertise in our team. We recruit on merit, actively seek diverse applicant pools and encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply. We do not discriminate on the basis of disability, age, gender identity and expression, national origin, race and ethnicity, religious beliefs, marital or parental status, or sexual orientation, and welcome all types of diversity.

Project Slingshot is a global nonprofit organization dedicated to ending factory farming. We do this by exposing the lies, cruelty, and power of Big Ag through disruptive campaigns that cut through the noise, capture public attention, and build unstoppable momentum for change.

The Role
As Digital Marketing Director (US) you will lead our US marketing strategy, making sure our campaigns are not just seen, but felt. You'll build and run high-impact digital, email and paid media programs that mobilize supporters, grow audiences, and put Slingshot in front of the people who can shift this fight.
You'll work closely with our global team, but with the autonomy to localize and innovate for the US context - ensuring every piece of content, every email and every ad campaign resonates, drives action, and delivers ambitious, measurable outcomes. You will know how to leverage cultural moments that help to seed marketing narratives among targeted audiences, and influence them to act.
In this role you will manage a Digital Marketing & Social Media Manager to help drive engagement across our marketing and social activities in support of our campaign efforts.
This is a remote position based in the US.
What You'll Do
Digital strategy & execution

  • Localize global campaign moments for the US market without losing the force of the original idea.
  • Own the US marketing calendar and make sure it lines up with campaign and creative plans.
Email & CRM

  • Build automations and journeys that nurture supporters through the funnel.
  • Constantly refine audience segmentation and personalization.
  • Partner with fundraising to make sure marketing and giving journeys reinforce each other.
Content & storytelling
  • Oversee creation of disruptive, compelling and on-brand digital content (copy, visuals, video).
  • Craft impactful storytelling and copywriting that inspires, provokes and mobilizes.
  • Ensure consistency and quality across all channels.
  • Brief and work closely with our creative team to turn campaign strategy into work that travels.
  • Cultivate influences relationships, partnerships and collaborations that deliver innovative story telling and expand audience reach and engagement.
Analytics & optimization
  • Monitor KPIs across social, email and digital campaigns.
  • Produce actionable insights from analytics to inform strategy.
  • Use performance data to test, iterate and continually improve.
  • Report clearly to leadership on what is working, what is not, and what you are changing as a result.
Leadership & collaboration
  • Build and mentor a Digital Marketing & Social Media Manager.
  • Collaborate closely with global colleagues to align strategies, share learnings and identify opportunities.
  • Ensure US digital campaigns amplify and complement Project Slingshot's global campaigns.
  • Manage agency, freelance, influencer and platform relationships in the US market.

Requirements

We'd love someone who:
  • Has significant experience in digital marketing, campaign strategy or movement-building - ideally with a cause-driven brand or a bold advocacy group.
  • Is deeply familiar with social justice messaging, digital organizing and content-led engagement strategies.
  • Has led teams and knows how to develop teams to deliver results.
  • Has proven success in social media, paid ads and email/CRM strategies.
  • Knows META Ads Manager, email marketing platforms (e.g. GetResponse, Mailchimp, Campaign Monitor or similar), analytics tools and automation systems in depth.
  • Is skilled at using audience insights to craft strategies that inspire action.
  • Writes strong copy, with a knack for storytelling that is bold, disruptive and emotionally compelling.
  • Has a track record of driving audience growth and measurable impact.
  • Is data-driven, experimental, and never satisfied with "good enough".
  • Brings knowledge or experience of farmed animal advocacy, broader animal protection, or high-profile nonprofit campaigning - with the ability to translate complex issues into powerful, public-facing narratives.
  • Is passionate about Project Slingshot's mission and hungry to play a part in ending factory farming.
Success looks like
  • Growing audience size and engagement across platforms, with clear evidence of what is driving it.
  • Lead acquisition, conversion rates and supporter retention are all improving.
  • High-impact US campaigns are landing - measured in reach, earned media and actions taken.
  • Internal marketing processes are strong and cross-team collaboration is working without friction.
  • Slingshot has real cultural presence and brand salience across US social justice spaces.

Benefits

Location & Working Pattern
This role is remote and based in the United States. Project Slingshot is a fully remote organization. Most collaboration happens online, and you will have regular overlap with colleagues in the UK. There will occasionally be opportunities and expectations to travel for team meet-ups, campaign shoots, conferences, planning sessions and other in-person events. jobs.excerpt: Job Description Summary‎ The Vice President, Total Rewards will lead the strategy, design, and delivery of Mosaic Health’s enterprise compensation and benefits programs.
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary

‎

The Vice President, Total Rewards will lead the strategy, design, and delivery of Mosaic Health’s enterprise compensation and benefits programs. Reporting to the Chief People Officer, this executive will bring Compensation and Benefits together under an integrated Total Rewards strategy that supports business performance, strengthens Mosaic Health’s ability to attract and retain critical talent, and advances the organization’s continued evolution as one integrated company.

Serving as a trusted advisor to senior leaders, the Vice President will shape compensation, executive rewards, incentives, benefits strategy, market competitiveness, and rewards governance while driving greater consistency, scalability, and effectiveness across the enterprise. This leader will also oversee rewards harmonization, executive compensation, compensation planning, M&A integration, and the continued use of analytics, technology, automation, and AI to strengthen decision-making and employee experience.

The ideal candidate is a strategic, business-minded, and analytically rigorous Total Rewards executive who can influence at the highest levels, simplify complexity, lead through transformation, and build a high-performing, integrated Total Rewards function.

‎

How will you make an impact & Requirements

‎

What You’ll Do

  • Develop and execute Mosaic Health’s enterprise Total Rewards strategy across compensation, benefits, executive rewards, and related programs.
  • Lead compensation strategy, including base pay, annual incentives, executive compensation, market benchmarking, salary structures, and job architecture.
  • Lead benefits strategy across health, welfare, retirement, and wellbeing programs, balancing market competitiveness, employee value, cost, and long-term sustainability.
  • Establish strong Total Rewards governance, decision rights, and consistent, market-based compensation practices.
  • Partner closely with the Chief People Officer, CEO, CFO, and other senior leaders on significant compensation and rewards decisions.
  • Support executive compensation governance and Human Capital/Compensation Committee activities.
  • Lead annual compensation planning and continue to strengthen compensation technology, analytics, and processes.
  • Develop and execute strategies to harmonize rewards programs across Mosaic Health while thoughtfully managing talent, cost, organizational, and employee impacts.
  • Lead Total Rewards due diligence and integration activities associated with mergers and acquisitions.
  • Leverage data, market intelligence, technology, automation, and AI to improve decision-making, employee experience, and operational efficiency.
  • Lead, develop, and integrate the Compensation and Benefits teams into a high-performing, enterprise-focused Total Rewards function.
  • Build scalable operating practices, controls, and processes that support Mosaic Health’s continued growth and evolution.

What You’ll Bring

  • 12+ years of progressive experience in Total Rewards, Compensation, Benefits, or related HR leadership roles
  • Significant enterprise-level compensation experience, including incentive design, market benchmarking, salary structures, and compensation governance
  • Experience leading or providing significant strategic oversight of employee benefits programs
  • Demonstrated experience with executive compensation and supporting senior executive decision-making
  • Strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to connect rewards strategy and investments to business performance and talent outcomes
  • Demonstrated ability to advise, influence, and constructively challenge senior executives on complex and sensitive issues
  • Strong analytical orientation with the ability to use market data, financial analysis, and workforce insights to develop recommendations and evaluate tradeoffs
  • Demonstrated success leading teams through organizational growth, transformation, and change
  • Experience working within a complex, multi-site, healthcare, services, or similarly distributed organization preferred
  • Experience supporting mergers, acquisitions, and Total Rewards integration strongly preferred
  • Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree or relevant professional certification preferred

How You Lead

Enterprise-minded: You optimize Total Rewards strategies and decisions for Mosaic Health as a whole rather than for individual legacy organizations.

Business-oriented: You connect compensation and benefits decisions directly to business performance, workforce priorities, and talent outcomes.

Strategic and pragmatic: You establish a compelling long-term direction while making practical, thoughtful near-term decisions.

Analytically rigorous: You use market data, financial analysis, and workforce insights to shape recommendations and evaluate tradeoffs.

Influential: You build credibility with senior leaders and are comfortable advising, influencing, and constructively challenging executives.

Operationally disciplined: You establish clear governance, accountability, controls, and scalable processes.

Transformation-oriented: You challenge legacy practices, simplify complexity, and build capabilities that position Mosaic Health for the future.

Collaborative: You build strong partnerships across the People organization, Finance, business leadership, and other key stakeholders to advance enterprise priorities.

What Success Looks Like

In this role, early success will mean creating greater clarity, consistency, and enterprise alignment across Mosaic Health’s Total Rewards programs. Key priorities include:

  • Establishing an integrated enterprise Total Rewards philosophy and strategy.
  • Bringing Compensation and Benefits together under one leadership and operating model.
  • Strengthening market benchmarking, job architecture, and compensation infrastructure.
  • Advancing incentive and executive compensation strategy and governance.
  • Continuing to optimize Mosaic Health’s benefits offerings and cost structure.
  • Establishing a clear and sustainable approach to rewards harmonization across the organization.
  • Improving compensation planning through technology, analytics, automation, and AI.
  • Building a strong, integrated Total Rewards team with clear roles, governance, and operating practices.

Why Mosaic Health?

Mosaic Health is committed to building an inclusive workplace where talented individuals from diverse backgrounds can thrive. We believe better care begins with empowered people, collaborative teams, and leaders who are passionate about improving the health of the communities we serve.


If you're energized by solving complex problems, influencing enterprise-wide strategy, and helping shape the future of healthcare delivery, we'd love to hear from you.

jobs.title: Grantmaking Strategy Development Consultancy
jobs.excerpt: About Urgent Action Fund for Feminist Activism Urgent Action Fund for Feminist Activism partners with frontline feminist movements to support women, trans, and non-binary activists who take and face enormous risks to challenge oppressive systems and build a more just and equitable world.
jobs.companyName: Urgent Action Fund for Feminist Activism
jobs.description:
About Urgent Action Fund for Feminist Activism

Urgent Action Fund for Feminist Activism partners with frontline feminist movements to support women, trans, and non-binary activists who take and face enormous risks to challenge oppressive systems and build a more just and equitable world. Our holistic, flexible approach enables frontline feminists to respond to real-time threats and opportunities, protect and care for themselves and one another, and sustain and propel solutions to the most critical crises and injustices of our time.

Founded in 1997, Urgent Action Fund for Feminist Activism is one of four independent Urgent Action Sister Funds that share and build power collectively on behalf of frontline feminists worldwide. Based in the United States, Urgent Action Fund for Feminist Activism supports individuals, organizations and movements in the Middle East, Europe, the Balkans, the Caucasus, Turkey, Central Asia, Russia, Canada and the U.S. Together with our Sister Funds – who resource feminist activists in Africa, Asia and the Pacific, and Latin America and the Caribbean – we seek to provide an interconnected tapestry of flexible support to feminist movements globally.

Background

Over the past two years, the Programs Team has engaged in a series of internal planning discussions to articulate the purpose, vision, and desired outcomes of a long-term grantmaking strategy. These discussions established the rationale for strategy development, the outcomes it should achieve, and the collaborative principles that will guide its development. Additionally, UAF has begun processes to develop an overarching organizational strategy, including the refinement and articulation of UAF’s political identity, vision, values, and voice. The grantmaking strategy will be both an expression of an emerging broader organizational strategy and an important input into its future development. Furthermore, the grantmaking strategy is pivotal to ensuring that in the current institutional moment, UAF can continue to make strategic progress while recognizing that the broader organizational strategy will continue to develop as we learn from implementation, the changing environment, and our institutional experience.

The consultant/s will support UAF in translating this foundation into a comprehensive, future-oriented grantmaking strategy that reflects the organization's feminist values, movement partnerships, operational realities, and long-term vision.

Purpose of the Assignment

The purpose of this consultancy is to support UAF in developing a five-year grantmaking strategy that:

  • articulates a clear grantmaking vision and strategic direction;
  • strengthens organizational decision-making during periods of uncertainty and crisis;
  • clarifies grantmaking priorities, approaches, and funding modalities;
  • aligns grantmaking with feminist organizational values and broader institutional priorities;
  • supports learning, adaptation, and continuous reflection;
  • positions UAF to respond effectively to evolving movement, political, and philanthropic contexts.

Objectives

  • Design and facilitate an inclusive, participatory, and feminist strategy development process.
  • Review and synthesize existing organizational strategies, grantmaking data, evaluations, and learning products to reflect our institutional knowledge.
  • Conduct environmental scanning and landscape analysis relevant to feminist philanthropy, crisis response, movement ecosystems, and emerging global trends.
  • Develop and facilitate meaningful approaches to internal and external engagement, ensuring that relevant perspectives from staff, leadership, movement, partners, advisors, and other stakeholders inform the strategy throughout the process.
  • Surface strategic opportunities, assumptions, tensions, and decision points requiring organizational discussion.
  • Support future-oriented scenario planning.
  • Translate emerging strategic decisions and iterative feedback into a coherent five-year Grantmaking Strategy.
  • Support the development of an implementation approach, learning framework, and adaptation process.

Scope of Work

The consultant will support UAF through a collaborative strategy development process spanning approximately 15 months.

UAF expects the consultancy to encompass the broad areas of work outlined below. While they are presented in a general progression, UAF recognizes that an effective strategy development process is likely to be iterative rather than linear. These areas reflect the key outcomes and deliverables UAF expects the process to address and are not intended to prescribe a specific methodology, sequence, or duration.

Applicants are encouraged to propose how they would structure the process within the overall consultancy period, including the sequencing and potential overlap of work areas, the time allocated to different components, methods, and engagement approaches, and any interim outputs they believe would strengthen the process. In particular, UAF does not expect internal or external engagement to occur only at a single stage of the process. Relevant perspectives may need to be engaged at different points to inform discovery, explore strategic questions, test emerging directions, and refine the strategy.

The final methodology, workplan, timeline, sequencing, and engagement approach will be refined and agreed upon with UAF during project initiation.

Project Initiation and Alignment

This area of work will establish a shared foundation for the strategy development process and ensure alignment between UAF and the consultant on the purpose, scope, approach, roles, and expectations for the work.

Key Outcomes:

  • A strong shared understanding of UAF’s organizational context, previous planning, and relevant background informing the strategy development process.
  • An agreed methodology that reflects UAF’s context, needs, and intended outcomes for the strategy development process.
  • Clear roles, responsibilities, governance, communication, and decision-making arrangements for the process.
  • A clear and realistic work plan and timeline for completing the strategy development process.
  • A meaningful and appropriate approach to engaging relevant staff, leadership, partners, and other stakeholders throughout the process.

Key Deliverables:

  • Final methodology and work plan
  • Engagement approach and project timeline.

Discovery and Learning

This read of work will develop a shared understanding of UAF’s current grantmaking approach, organizational learning, and the broader context in which UAF operates.

The consultant will support the Programs Team in identifying and exploring the evidence, perspectives, and strategic questions that should inform the development of the strategy.

Key Outcomes:

  • A synthesized understanding of UAF's grantmaking experience, strengths, challenges, patterns, and learning.
  • Greater understanding of relevant external trends and their implications for UAF's future grantmaking.
  • Identification of key strategic questions, assumptions, tensions, opportunities, and areas requiring further exploration.
  • A shared evidence base to inform strategic discussions and decisions throughout the process.

Key Deliverables:

  • Discovery and learning synthesis.
  • Relevant external landscape analysis.
  • Identification of key strategic questions and areas for further exploration.

Strategy Development

This area of work will translate learning from the discovery process into potential strategic directions and begin developing the grantmaking strategy.

Key Outcomes:

  • Clear articulation of the major strategic choices facing UAF.
  • Exploration of potential strategic priorities and directions, including relevant opportunities, risks, tensions, and trade-offs.
  • Greater organizational alignment around an emerging direction for UAF's grantmaking.
  • Translation of emerging strategic decisions into an initial strategy.

Key Deliverables:

  • Strategic synthesis and recommendations
  • Initial draft of the Grantmaking Strategy

External Engagement and Refinement

External perspectives should meaningfully inform the development of the strategy rather than serve solely as a final validation exercise. Engagement with partners, advisors, movements, peer organizations, and other relevant stakeholders may therefore take place at different points throughout the consultancy, depending on the methodology proposed by the consultant and agreed with UAF.

This area of work should ensure that UAF's emerging thinking is informed by movement realities and relevant external perspectives and that key assumptions and strategic directions can be appropriately explored and tested.

Key Outcomes:

  • Relevant movement and stakeholder perspectives meaningfully inform the strategy.
  • Key assumptions, priorities, and emerging strategic directions are tested against relevant external perspectives.
  • Areas of alignment, challenge, opportunity, and further consideration are identified.
  • External engagement strengthens rather than simply validates UAF's strategic thinking.

The consultant should propose an appropriate approach to external engagement, including which perspectives to engage, when in the process, and by which methods.

Key Deliverables:

  • Synthesis of relevant external perspectives
  • Recommendations for refinement of the emerging strategy.
  • Updated draft of the Grantmaking Strategy

Organizational Sensemaking, Review and Refinement

Internal engagement and sense-making will similarly occur throughout the strategy development process. This area of work reflects the need for dedicated opportunities to bring together learning, test emerging choices, address areas of disagreement or uncertainty, and build sufficient organizational ownership around the strategy.

Key Outcomes:

  • Relevant staff and leadership perspectives meaningfully inform the development of the strategy.
  • Strategic priorities, choices, trade-offs, and implications are sufficiently understood across relevant parts of UAF.
  • Areas requiring further discussion, decision, or refinement are surfaced and addressed.
  • Organizational ownership and alignment are strengthened without requiring artificial consensus on every issue.
  • Initial implications for implementation are understood.

Key Deliverables:

  • Revised Grantmaking Strategy reflecting relevant organizational input.
  • High-level implementation considerations.

Finalization

This area of work will result in a finalized five-year Grantmaking Strategy and position UAF to move effectively from strategy development into implementation, learning, and adaptation.

Key Outcomes:

  • Organizational agreement on UAF's five-year grantmaking vision, strategic direction, priorities, and approach.
  • Clear understanding of the implications of the strategy for implementation.
  • An appropriate framework for learning from, monitoring, and adapting the strategy over time.
  • Staff and leadership are prepared to transition from strategy development to implementation.

Key Deliverables:

  • Final Grantmaking Strategy
  • High-level implementation roadmap
  • Learning, monitoring, and adaptation framework
  • Final presentation and handover

Overall Deliverables

The key deliverables anticipated across the areas of work are identified above. Applicants may recommend modifications to the format, sequencing, or combination of interim deliverables if they believe an alternative approach would better support the process's intended outcomes.

The final five-year Grantmaking Strategy, high-level implementation roadmap, and learning, monitoring, and adaptation framework are the required final deliverables.

Applicants are encouraged to propose additional or alternative interim outputs they believe would add value to the process. The specific format and sequencing of interim deliverables will be refined and agreed upon with UAF during project initiation.

Working Principles

The consultant is expected to work in ways that are:

  • Participatory and collaborative.
  • Feminist and care-centered.
  • Movement-informed.
  • Equity-driven.
  • Reflective and adaptive.
  • Inclusive of multiple perspectives and ways of knowing.

The consultant will facilitate discussion and provide recommendations while recognizing that all strategic decisions remain the responsibility of UAF.

Roles and Governance

The strategy development process will be coordinated through a distributed leadership model.

The Programs Team will contribute expertise based on thematic portfolios, regional leadership, institutional knowledge, learning and evaluation, partnerships, and collective care.

The consultant will work closely with the UAF Grantmaking Managing Officer and the Director of Programs, engage with the broader Programs Team as subject-matter experts throughout the process, and collaborate with other UAF teams and external stakeholders as appropriate.

Requirements

Who We Are Looking For

We are seeking a consultant or consulting team with demonstrated experience facilitating complex strategy development processes within philanthropy, civil society, or social justice organizations.

The ideal consultant will bring:

  • Experience facilitating organizational and grantmaking strategy development.
  • Strong understanding of feminist movements, feminist philanthropy, participatory grantmaking, and movement-building approaches.
  • Demonstrated ability to design and facilitate participatory processes that build shared ownership and support collective decision-making.
  • Experience integrating learning, monitoring, evaluation (MEL), adaptive management, and organizational learning into strategy development processes.
  • Experience conducting qualitative research, environmental scans, stakeholder consultations, and strategic analysis, with the ability to synthesize complex information into clear, practical, and actionable recommendations.
  • Experience working with international grantmaking organizations, foundations, or intermediary funders.
  • Experience working effectively with diverse, multicultural, multilingual, and geographically dispersed stakeholders across multiple time zones.
  • High levels of flexibility, adaptability, cultural humility, and comfort navigating complex and evolving strategic conversations.
  • Demonstrated cultural humility, political awareness, confidentiality, and discretion when working with diverse feminist movements and stakeholders across different regional and geopolitical contexts.

Benefits

Consultancy budget: USD $75,000

Duration: Approximately 15 months

Anticipated start date: January 4, 2027

Application deadline: November 31, 2026

Location: Remote

Working language: English

Working arrangements: The consultant or team must be able to accommodate meetings and collaboration across U.S. Eastern and Pacific Time zones.

Reporting to: Grantmaking Managing Officer and Director of Programs, Urgent Action Fund for Feminist Activism.

Questions: For questions about the consultancy or application process, please contact Johnny Tohme at . Applications must be submitted through this posting and will not be accepted by email.

Are you an Apache Kafka committer who wants to operate at the highest level of technical and community influence? You will work at both levels - upstream influence and customer impact - with meaningful autonomy, strong peer collaboration, and direct access to the product and field relationships that turn technical work into commercial outcomes. Postion location: US REMOTE

Overview

As a Senior Open Source Software Engineer, your responsibilities will include:

  • Lead end-to-end upstream initiatives in Apache Kafka, from KIP authoring and design consensus through implementation, review, and release, in domains such as broker internals, storage and log management, replication, KRaft metadata quorum, consumer group coordination, Kafka Streams, Kafka Connect, observability, and release quality.
  • Provide binding committer reviews on upstream patches and community contributions, applying the technical rigor and authority that moves high-quality work through the Apache Kafka review process.
  • Contribute to Apache Kafka release management as part of the committer community, including release planning, blocker triage, test stabilization, release candidate validation, documentation readiness, and post-release follow-through.
  • Translate enterprise customer and operator needs into credible upstream proposals, KIP-level designs, and sustained technical engagement that only a committer can supply; advise product and field teams on complex Kafka trade-offs.

  • Mentor engineers toward committer standing and raise overall contribution quality through rigorous review practices, test discipline, and clear engineering guidance.
  • Improve upstream infrastructure, including CI reliability, test coverage, contributor tooling, benchmarking, release automation, and compatibility validation, to reduce project-wide maintenance burden.

Job Requirements

  • A minimum of 12 years of applicable professional software engineering experience is required.
  • Current Apache Kafka committer status with a sustained and publicly verifiable upstream track record across patches, reviews, KIPs, and community standing in Kafka core or a closely related area such as Streams, Connect, clients, or release engineering.
  • Expert Java engineering capability in performance-sensitive, concurrent, and production-grade distributed systems, with the ability to write, review, and reason about complex Kafka internals at depth.
  • Deep mastery of Apache Kafka internals in at least one major domain: broker storage and log replication, KRaft and metadata management, consumer group coordination and rebalancing, protocol and client compatibility, Kafka Streams, Kafka Connect, observability, performance, or release management and CI.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex technical work through the Apache open source governance model: KIP authoring or co-sponsorship, design consensus, mailing-list engagement, and Jira-driven delivery from proposal through merge.
  • Strong written communication for asynchronous, global, public technical collaboration - mailing lists, design documents, code reviews, and Jira threads.
  • Proven senior-level technical judgment that resolves most blockers independently, determines approach on novel or ambiguous assignments, surfaces systemic risks proactively, and produces work that is consistent with project and team objectives.

Preferred qualifications

  • PMC membership in Apache Kafka or a related Apache project.
  • Track record of work in current Kafka feature and maintenance areas such as KRaft maturity, controller and metadata reliability, consumer rebalance protocol improvements, exactly-once semantics, tiered storage, Kafka Connect security and operability, Streams APIs, client metrics, or release stabilization.
  • Experience connecting upstream technical leadership to enterprise customer and operator outcomes - translating production pain points into accepted community improvements.
  • History of mentoring contributors toward reviewer or committer standing in an open governance project.
  • Familiarity with the Kafka ecosystem: Kafka Streams, Kafka Connect, MirrorMaker 2, Kafka clients, schema and serialization patterns, Kubernetes-based Kafka operations, or adjacent open source projects such as Strimzi.

Education

Bachelor's degree in engineering or technical related field of study Or additional equivalent experience.

Team Information

Leadership and team culture

The hiring manager for this role is an Engineering Manager for the Open Source Engineering team. You will join a globally distributed group that values committer-grade technical judgment, clear ownership, transparent community engagement, and practical impact on real customer outcomes.

The team culture is high-trust and high-accountability. We support engineers who can go deep technically, mentor others generously, collaborate across product and field functions, and improve both code and the contributor ecosystem around it. You will have significant autonomy paired with close collaboration and genuine visibility into the strategic bets your work enables.

Enterprise Sales Director

Are you a top-performing sales hunter ready to deliver results in the Oracle & SAP support market?

We’re looking for an Enterprise Sales Director to drive new business growth in the third-party support market for Oracle & SAP across the UK and EMEA. This isn’t about managing accounts or inheriting existing clients, this is pure, ground-up sales in a high-growth sector. We’re scaling rapidly and expanding our enterprise sales capability, and we need proven closers who know how to win.

If you’ve worked in the third-party support industry or have experience selling alternative support solutions to Oracle and SAP clients, this is your opportunity to take a leading role in a market with significant growth potential.
This is a full-time, fully remote UK role.

What you’ll be doing:
  • Owning and expanding the Oracle & SAP third-party support market across the UK and EMEA
  • Representing Support Revolution at client meetings, conferences and networking events, maintaining a smart and professional appearance
  • Building relationships with C-level executives and IT decision-makers

What we’re looking for:
  • 5+ years success in Enterprise sales, ideally in third-party software support
  • A demonstrated ability to consistently beat quota in a competitive market
  • A hunter mindset - you build pipelines from scratch and close net-new logos
  • The ability to navigate complex enterprise sales cycles and win big deals

Interview process:

Our hiring process is designed to be efficient and transparent. Here’s what to expect:

We offer a competitive salary and a comprehensive benefits package, including:

  • Company Pension Scheme: Secure your future with our Company pension scheme
  • Perkbox Perks: Treat yourself with discounts, cashback, and wellness benefits
  • Fully Remote Model: Enjoy the flexibility of working 100% remotely, from wherever you are in the UK - no office required!
  • Employee Wellbeing: We’ve got your back with EAP, eye tests, flu vouchers, and excellent sick pay if you’re ever unwell
  • Personal Development: We invest in you with tailored training and career growth
  • Employee Referral Scheme: Get rewarded for bringing great talent to our team.

At Support Revolution, we help organisations break free from overpriced software support and forced upgrades, slashing maintenance costs while delivering superior service. Our mission is to empower businesses to reallocate savings into innovation, fuelling their growth.

Job Description

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline and portfolio of medicines to treat heart disease, obesity and obesity-related conditions, rare diseases, inflammatory conditions and cancer. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

Internal Meetings Manager, U.S. Commercial

What you will do

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this vital role you will manage internal off-site meetings for Amgen’s U.S. Commercial organization. This includes national meetings, POAs, launch and brand planning meetings, leadership summits, functional meetings, training programs, and other internal events across Commercial business units.

The Manager oversees end-to-end meeting strategy, execution, budgeting, risk management, and vendor partnerships, ensuring all programs align with Amgen’s priorities, compliance standards, and GMM processes. The role drives consistency, resource optimization, technology adoption, and continuous improvement across the internal meetings portfolio.

This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports, reporting to the GMM Sr. Manager, U.S. Region. Strong collaboration with cross-functional partners and outsourced suppliers is essential to delivering high-quality, compliant, and cost-effective meetings. Travel is required (approximately 30%-40%).

Responsibilities

  • Serve as a trusted advisor to stakeholders on meeting policies, planning, and best practices.

  • Build strong partnerships with business leaders and meeting sponsors to support business objectives.
  • Drive operational excellence, standardization, and continuous improvement across meeting programs.
  • Support change management, process enhancements, and technology adoption initiatives.

We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The strategic professional we seek is a collaborative leader with these qualifications.

Doctorate degree

What you can expect from us

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

Controller Job Description

Company: Pro Coffee Gear
Location: Remote (Global)
Employment Type: Full-time

About Us

Pro Coffee Gear is a rapidly growing e-commerce company specializing in espresso machines and related parts. Our passion for coffee drives us to provide top-tier products and exceptional customer service to coffee enthusiasts worldwide. With a dedication to quality and innovation, we aim to elevate the coffee experience for our customers and become a leading authority in the industry. As a dynamic and diverse team, we value collaboration, creativity, and continuous improvement, and we're committed to fostering a positive and inclusive work environment where everyone can thrive.
