The ideal candidate will have extensive experience in financial management, reporting, and analysis, with the ability to drive financial strategy and provide executive-level insights to support business growth and decision-making.

Responsibilities

Financial Management & Reporting

  • Oversee all aspects of financial operations including Accounts Payable (AP), Accounts Receivable (AR), and Payroll management
  • Lead monthly, quarterly, and annual financial close processes with accuracy and timeliness
  • Prepare and present comprehensive financial statements, management reports, and board-level presentations
  • Develop and maintain robust financial controls, policies, and procedures to ensure compliance and accuracy

Strategic Analysis & Planning

  • Provide strategic financial analysis and recommendations to executive leadership
  • Lead annual budgeting and forecasting processes, including variance analysis and performance metrics
  • Develop sophisticated financial models and pro forma analyses for business initiatives, product launches, and strategic investments
  • Conduct profitability analysis by product line, customer segment, and business unit

Systems Integration & Process Optimization

  • Ensure seamless integration of inventory management, e-commerce platforms, and payment systems with the general ledger
  • Lead ERP system optimization and financial system implementations
  • Drive process improvement initiatives to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and scalability
  • Establish and maintain key performance indicators (KPIs) and financial dashboards

Compliance & Risk Management

  • Manage relationships with external auditors, tax professionals, and regulatory bodies
  • Ensure compliance with US GAAP, tax regulations, and reporting requirements
  • Oversee internal controls and SOX compliance (if applicable)
  • Identify and mitigate financial risks across the organization

Team Leadership & Development

  • Lead and mentor finance team members, fostering professional growth and development
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with operations, sales, marketing, and executive teams
  • Provide financial training and support to non-finance departments

Requirements

Education & Certifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field required
  • CPA certification strongly preferred
  • Master's degree in Accounting, Finance, or MBA preferred

Experience

  • Minimum 7-10 years of progressive accounting and finance experience
  • At least 3-5 years in a Controller or senior financial management role
  • Experience in e-commerce, retail, or inventory-based businesses strongly preferred
  • Public accounting experience with Big 4 or mid-tier firms is a plus

Technical Skills

  • Advanced expertise in Excel, Google Sheets, and financial modeling
  • Proficiency with ERP systems (NetSuite, QuickBooks Enterprise, SAP, etc.)
  • Experience with e-commerce platforms and inventory management systems
  • Strong understanding of business intelligence and reporting tools

Core Competencies

  • Deep understanding of US GAAP and IFRS accounting principles
  • Comprehensive knowledge of US tax system, regulations, and reporting deadlines
  • Proven track record of successful month-end and year-end close processes
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities with attention to detail
  • Experience in process improvement and change management
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills for executive-level reporting

Work Requirements

  • Must align with Central Time business hours for collaboration with US-based team
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, remote environment with minimal supervision
  • Strong project management skills and ability to handle multiple priorities

Benefits

  • Opportunities for career growth and advancement within a rapidly expanding company
  • Remote work with flexible hours, allowing for healthy work-life balance
  • Goal-oriented work culture providing autonomy and opportunities for personal and professional development

How to Apply

If you're an experienced finance leader with a passion for driving business growth and a love for coffee, we want to hear from you! Join us in shaping the future of coffee and contributing to our company's continued growth and success.

Ongoing long-term position (minimum 12-month commitment) Must be able to commit to making regular scheduled calls to participants, generally once per week Flexible calling schedule based on volunteer and participant availability Volunteer from your own home Typical calls range from 20 minutes to 1 hour Statement of Volunteer Service available after 12 months Centrelink confirmation of volunteer hours available Commitment to participate in mandatory training and ongoing learning requirements

Why Choose to Volunteer with Red Cross?

Help reduce loneliness and social isolation in your community Gain valuable communication and interpersonal skills Receive comprehensive training and ongoing support Join Australia's largest humanitarian network Volunteer flexibly from home, with opportunities to participate in office-based activities and events when available

The Program Social connection is vital for overall wellbeing. Telechat is an Australian Red Cross social support program designed to reduce social isolation through regular telephone conversations. Participants are matched with a dedicated volunteer based on shared interests and preferences, helping to build trusted relationships through ongoing conversations, companionship and meaningful social connection. From the comfort of your own home, you can help people stay connected to their community and enjoy a sense of friendship and belonging. The Opportunity We are seeking friendly, compassionate and reliable volunteers to join our Telechat program. Volunteers are matched with a participant and make regular scheduled calls at a mutually agreed time, generally once per week. Calls typically range from 20 minutes to 1 hour and focus on building rapport, providing companionship and creating meaningful social connections. Training and ongoing support are provided to help you succeed in the role. Key Requirements & Your Commitment

Be willing to join a nationwide team delivering a social inclusion program within Aged and Community Care. Make friendly and engaging social support calls to a matched participant. Build rapport and meaningful connections through regular conversations. Possess excellent communication and active listening skills. Help reduce social isolation through companionship and conversation. Respect the privacy, rights and dignity of participants and maintain confidentiality. Complete a simple call record after each conversation. Follow privacy, safeguarding and escalation procedures. Report any concerns regarding participant wellbeing to the Telechat team. Utilise email, online forms and basic digital systems as required. Maintain clear professional relationships and appropriate boundaries. Participate in mandatory learning and development activities. Commit to upholding Red Cross policies, the Aged Care Code of Conduct and any related requirements. Demonstrate cultural sensitivity and provide inclusive support to people from diverse backgrounds.

Red Cross will ensure you have training, ongoing support and access to other opportunities within the world's largest humanitarian network. The Impact As a Telechat volunteer, you'll provide more than conversation. You'll offer companionship, connection and a trusted relationship that can help reduce loneliness and support people to remain connected to their community. Every call has the potential to create meaningful connection, improve wellbeing and bring friendship and belonging into someone's life. In return, you'll gain valuable insights, develop your communication skills and experience the reward of making a genuine difference through simple, purposeful conversations. Application Requirements

Access to your own computer, laptop or smartphone. Reliable phone and internet connection. All volunteers will be required to undertake a National Police Check, organised through Red Cross. Statutory Declaration to be completed if you have been a citizen or permanent resident of a country other than Australia after turning 16 years of age. Willingness to comply with Red Cross and Aged Care Codes of Conduct. Commitment to maintaining professional boundaries and participant confidentiality.

Further Information To find out more about this opportunity please contact the Aged and Community Care Volunteer Assistance Team via email . Thank you for considering volunteering with Red Cross. We also have great career opportunities. Please visit: Purposeful conversations. Meaningful connections. Every call, every week.

jobs.description:
JOB PURPOSE:

The Outside Sales Representative (OSR) - Commercial & Industrial (C&I) is responsible for developing and growing a regional portfolio of C&I solar and energy storage (ESS) customers, including EPCs, developers, commercial installers, and other sophisticated project stakeholders. In addition, the OSR will support the rest of the sales team across their defined territory with key C&I opportunities, as needed, The C&I OSR leads consultative, solution-oriented sales efforts across longer and more complex project cycles, translating customer technical, commercial, procurement, and delivery requirements into tailored product and supply-chain solutions. By combining market expertise, disciplined account planning, accurate forecasting, and strong cross-functional execution, this role positions the company as the preferred distribution partner for C&I EPC/Developers as well as residential installers establishing C&I divisions.

This role reports to the Director of Sales, C&I Solar & Energy Storage.

PRIMARY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Develop and execute a regional C&I sales strategy and account plan to achieve revenue, gross margin, pipeline, and customer-acquisition objectives.
  • Prospect, qualify, and develop relationships with C&I EPCs, developers, commercial installers, and other project decision-makers and influencers.
  • Manage a portfolio of strategic and growth accounts, including opportunity mapping, stakeholder engagement, account penetration, retention, and share-of-wallet expansion.
  • Build and maintain a disciplined opportunity pipeline across the C&I project lifecycle, from early-stage design and budgeting through procurement, construction, and replenishment.
  • Conduct consultative discovery to understand project scope, schedule, technical specifications, commercial requirements, financing constraints, and supply-chain risks.
  • Develop coordinated products, pricing, logistics, credit, and inventory solutions that improve customer economics and project execution while protecting company margin and risk parameters.
  • Prepare and deliver professional customer presentations, proposals, product comparisons, and commercial recommendations to technical and executive audiences.
  • Maintain accurate CRM records, opportunity stages, close dates, probability assessments, forecasts, call plans, and account activity.
  • Coordinate with inside sales, commercial sales leadership, product management, procurement, credit, operations, branch teams, manufacturers, and technical resources to support product selection, solution development, project execution, and a consistent customer experience.
  • Monitor C&I market conditions, policy and incentive developments, product availability, and competitor activity to identify risks and growth opportunities.
  • Represent the company at customer meetings, industry events, trade shows, and regional networking activities.
  • Escalate material project, credit, service, or supply risks early and lead cross-functional resolution with a strong sense of ownership.

QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS:

  • Highly organized, self-directed, and commercially disciplined, with the ability to manage multiple accounts and complex opportunities over varying project timelines.
  • Demonstrated consultative-selling and strategic-account-management skills, including prospecting, relationship development, discovery, qualification, value articulation, negotiation, and closing across C&I EPCs, developers, commercial installers, and key project stakeholders. Ability to understand and discuss C&I solar and energy storage system architecture, major equipment categories, project economics, procurement considerations, and construction schedules at a commercially effective level.
  • Exceptional interpersonal, written, and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate complex recommendations effectively to technical, operational, procurement, finance, and executive audiences.
  • Ability to consistently achieve monthly, quarterly, and annual sales and gross-margin targets while maintaining forecast accuracy and accountability.

jobs.description:
Prominence Advisors is actively seeking an Account Executive to join our team.

As an Account Executive, you will be the long-term quarterback of some of Prominence's most important healthcare relationships. You'll inherit a book of established accounts and be accountable for named-account ownership, expansion revenue, and strategic account planning across a blended portfolio spanning Strategic, Growth, and Transactional accounts. This is a revenue-focused account management role. You'll sell Prominence's Epic Services and Analytics solutions to grow your accounts, with compensation tied to the revenue your book generates. You'll own the full sales cycle for every expansion opportunity in your book, and work alongside our Client Partnership Executives (CPEs), who lead new logo pursuits, so the customer experiences one continuous relationship. You will partner closely with Solution Engineering (SE) to architect and price technical solutions, and with our Delivery Success Owners (DSOs) to ensure every handoff into delivery carries full context. In this role, you'll become a trusted strategic advisor to our customers while consistently converting deep client insight into new opportunities.

Who We Are

Prominence is a healthcare and life sciences technology and consulting firm dedicated to helping leading organizations do more with their data. With deep expertise across the full ecosystem — spanning providers, payers, and life sciences — we turn complex data into actionable insight.

We deliver a full spectrum of services, including advisory, analytics, optimization, and IT staffing. Our work helps organizations operate more efficiently, improve patient outcomes, and deliver measurable financial impact through smarter use of data. Recognized as a 2x Best in KLAS organization, we partner with more than 120 health systems and 40 life sciences organizations, including 7 of the top 10 U.S. News & World Report-ranked institutions.

Through our life sciences brands, Tegra Analytics and WLH Consulting & Learning Solutions, we extend these capabilities to pharmaceutical and biotech organizations — combining data, consulting, and learning to advance commercial excellence.

By connecting strategy, data, and execution, we help organizations translate data into clarity, strategy into action, and vision into measurable results. At our core, we are a people-first, values-driven organization that believes strong teams and trusted partnerships are what ultimately make healthcare and life sciences smarter.

Job Summary

Essential Functions and Responsibilities

Revenue Growth & Pipeline Ownership:

  • Grow recognized revenue across your book of business by expanding Analytics and Epic Services work within each account
  • Build and manage a qualified pipeline of expansion and renewal opportunities, with disciplined CRM forecasting — accurate stage-gates, weighted pipeline, and close-date hygiene in Salesforce
  • Own the full sales cycle for expansion and partner sourced opportunities including discovery, solution shaping (with SE), proposal development, pricing, contract negotiation, up to close
  • Build a multi-year account management and growth plan for each named account, applying target segmentation and account segmentation methodology to prioritize where you invest time
  • Identify and pursue cross-sell and upsell opportunities across Prominence's Analytics and Epic Services solutions, managing SOW creation and opportunity management in Salesforce
  • Monitor customer contracts and lead renewals to protect and grow net revenue retention

Account & Relationship Ownership:

  • Serve as the single, long-term owner of every named account relationship, partnering with the CPE as new logos come on board, so the customer feels one continuous relationship rather than a handoff
  • Build, manage, and expand relationships with executive stakeholders (Director/VP/C-level) across a blended portfolio spanning Tier 1 (Strategic), Tier 2 (Growth), and Tier 3 (Transactional) accounts
  • Set up and lead customer-facing Quarterly Business Reviews, including at least one onsite annually for Tier 1 Strategic accounts
  • Prioritize your time across your book based on each account's tier and growth potential
  • Maintain current relationship mapping for each account — decision makers, influencers, and champions — in shared CRM dashboards

Cross-Functional Partnership & Handoffs:

  • Partner with Solution Engineering (SE) on every expansion pursuit to scope, architect, and price technical solutions
  • Own the Sales to Implementation handoff to the Delivery Success Owner (DSO), ensuring delivery receives full account context and deal history rather than a cold handoff
  • Act as the accountable owner for strategic and relationship-related escalations, partnering with the DSO, who owns delivery-specific escalations
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Marketing, Partnerships, and Delivery to grow accounts and surface new opportunities
  • Provide structured feedback to CPE, SE, and leadership on what's resonating with customers, to sharpen offerings and messaging

Forecasting, Performance & Escalation Management:

  • Maintain accurate, current pipeline and forecast data as an input to company-wide revenue planning
  • Contribute to high KLAS rankings and secure strong customer references through exceptional relationship management and delivery outcomes
  • Serve as a point of escalation for strategic and relationship-critical issues, intervening when necessary
  • Maintain a pulse on all active projects within your portfolio to proactively identify and mitigate account risk

Requirements

Education, Training and Experience

  • 5+ years of revenue-accountable account management or sales experience, ideally growing existing enterprise accounts, with a documented history of meeting or exceeding revenue or expansion targets
  • Demonstrated ownership of a full sales cycle: discovery, solution development, proposal, pricing, negotiation, and contract close
  • Experience managing a multi-account portfolio or territory against a defined revenue target, ideally $10M+ in owned or influenced annual revenue
  • Experience selling to or serving healthcare provider organizations preferred; working knowledge of Epic's EHR ecosystem and healthcare data & analytics is strongly preferred
  • Existing relationships with health system IT, analytics, or executive leaders preferred
  • Experience partnering with pre-sales or solutions engineering resources to scope and price complex, multi-stakeholder technical engagements
  • Proven track record of managing executive relationships and driving measurable revenue growth through strategic account management
  • Rigorous CRM discipline — accurate forecasting, pipeline hygiene, and stage-gate management in Salesforce or a comparable CRM
  • Exceptional problem-solving skills and the ability to construct creative, commercially sound solutions to complex client challenges
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build trust and rapport at the executive level
  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple competing priorities and stakeholders across a blended portfolio

Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities

  • Consultative: Leads with client strategy and insight rather than transactional selling; earns the right to propose solutions rather than pitching them.
  • Curious & Perceptive: Asks the second and third question, reads between the lines, and picks up on what customers aren't saying. Senses when something is off and brings the hustle to act on it before it becomes a problem.
  • Revenue-Driven & Accountable: Comfortable owning and being measured against a hard revenue number; treats forecast accuracy as a professional discipline, not an afterthought.
  • Professional: Demonstrates a high degree of professionalism by treating others with respect, keeping commitments, building trust within the team, working with integrity, and upholding organizational values (“Do Great Work and Move Mountains”).
  • Organized: Capable of managing multi-faceted work streams — pipeline, renewals, expansion pursuits, and delivery hand-offs — efficiently and in parallel.
  • Self-Motivated: Adept at managing personal schedules, meeting deadlines, and monitoring work quality independently against revenue goals.
  • Highly Adaptable: Quickly acclimates to new accounts, stakeholders, and deal contexts.
  • Creative: Approaches problems with a solution-oriented mindset, working collaboratively with SE to find novel, sellable solutions.
  • Communication: Effectively conveys clear and concise messages that resonate with the intended audience, both in written and verbal forms, including in high-stakes negotiations.
  • Proactive: Anticipates potential issues, addresses concerns before they escalate, and effectively raises them when necessary.
  • Team-Oriented: Partners seamlessly with CPE, SE, and DSO across every handoff, protecting continuity for the customer at each stage.

Physical and Medical Standards

Must be able to sit or stand at a computer and work independently, and to travel regularly.

Working Conditions and Environment

  • Must be able to sit or stand at a computer and work remotely and independently from a personal home office
  • Located near a major airport hub preferred for ease of travel
  • Ability to travel about once a month for onsite executive meetings, Quarterly Business Reviews, and industry conferences, particularly for Tier 1 Strategic accounts

Hours Worked

This is a Full Time, 40 hour per week position.

Benefits

Prominence is dedicated to hiring the best and brightest minds in healthcare and maintaining a culture that rewards our employees for following their passion. We are excited to offer the following benefits for this position:

  • Competitive Salaried and Hybrid Compensation Plans
  • Health Care Plan (Medical, HSAs, Dental & Vision)
  • Retirement Plan (401k)
  • Life Insurance (Basic, Voluntary & AD&D)
  • Dependent & Health Savings Accounts
  • Short Term & Long Term Disability
  • Paid Time Off (Vacation/Sick & Public Holidays)
  • Training & Development Fund
  • Work From Home
  • Charitable Giving to Causes You Believe In

Employment Eligibility

Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.

Commitment to Equal Opportunity

The world’s most talented professionals come from every background. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to age, race, color, religion, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, marital status, veteran or disability status, or any other characteristic protected by law. In addition, Prominence will provide reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities.

If you are smart and good at what you do, come as you are. All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply.

Partnership Eligibility

Our partnerships are extremely important to us. This online application is not intended for anyone who is currently under a non-compete agreement or has an arrangement that precludes employment at Prominence. We appreciate your help in respecting our partners.

Interested in learning more? Apply below to connect with our Talent team about immediate openings and future consulting projects.

Our Mission

Our mission is to SAVE AND IMPROVE LIVES BY EMPOWERING HEALTHCARE CONSUMERS. Come be part of remarkable.

Overview

How you can make a difference

As Senior Manager, Security Awareness & GRC, you will lead HealthEquity’s enterprise human risk management and security culture strategy. This role turns complex cybersecurity, fraud, privacy, compliance, and AI governance topics into clear, engaging, behavior-focused programs that help teammates recognize risk, make safer decisions, and protect our members, clients, partners, and business.

You will own the strategy, execution, measurement, and continuous improvement of enterprise security awareness programs, including phishing simulations, required training, teammate targeted education, new hire onboarding, executive messaging, internal and external security campaigns, and targeted communications for high-risk behaviors or emerging threats. You will partner closely with Security, GRC, Fraud, Privacy, Legal, HR, Marketing, Product Security, IT, and executive leadership to ensure security expectations are understood, actionable, and embedded into how work gets done.

This role requires a strategic communicator, program builder, creative campaign designer, and cross-functional influencer who can connect risk, behavior, culture, and business outcomes. You will create scalable awareness experiences, advise leaders on human risk trends, support audit and regulatory expectations, manage vendor and platform relationships, and use data to continuously strengthen HealthEquity’s security culture.

What you’ll be doing

  • Drive continuous improvement efforts by identifying opportunities for enhancing security governance, risk management, and compliance practices.
  • Drive HealthEquity’s enterprise security awareness and human risk management strategy, aligning teammate education, behavioral risk reduction, annual compliance expectations, and security culture priorities.
  • Design, launch, and continuously improve enterprise campaigns that drive measurable behavior change, including Cybersecurity Awareness Month, Internet Safety Month, Fraud Awareness Week, phishing awareness, AI governance education, and emerging threat communications.
  • Lead the creative development of security awareness campaigns, including campaign themes, visual concepts, messaging frameworks, presentation materials, social and intranet graphics, videos, newsletters, recognition assets, and teammate-facing engagement experiences.
  • Own the strategy and execution of phishing simulation programs, targeted learning, reporting workflows, reinforcement messaging, and recognition programs that encourage timely reporting and safer decisions.
  • Work with third party partners to create and maintain a range of security awareness educational materials, including e-learning modules, newsletters, posters, and videos, tailored to different audiences.
  • Establish metrics to assess the effectiveness of the security awareness program, including pre- and post-training evaluations, incident reports, and employee feedback.
  • Contribute in development and implementation of security metrics and key performance indicators (KPIs) to measure the effectiveness of security controls, risk mitigation strategies, and compliance efforts. Regularly analyze and report on security metrics to senior management, identifying trends, areas of improvement, and actionable insights.
  • Work closely with Security, IT, Fraud, Product, HR, Marketing, Legal, Privacy, and other departments to integrate security awareness into existing training and onboarding processes.
  • Ensure that security policies and procedures are effectively communicated and understood throughout the organization.
  • Collaborate with the Security Operations Center to provide guidance and support during security incidents, helping to educate employees on the importance of reporting suspicious activities.
  • Collaborate with security engineering organization to effectively identify and implement relevant tools and technologies to support the end to end human risk management of security awarness.
  • Lead through influence across cross-functional partners, balancing strategic program ownership with hands-on execution in a fast-paced, highly regulated environment.
  • Stay current on security threats, social engineering trends, AI risk, regulatory expectations, and awareness best practices to keep programs relevant, timely, and effective.
  • Advise leadership on human risk trends, communication risks, adoption barriers, and opportunities to improve security behavior across the enterprise.
  • Manage and mentor a team of security awareness specialists, fostering a collaborative and innovative environment.

  • Manage identification and rollout of scalable innovative technologies to support security governance, including developing usage policies and guidelines, audit, and control processes.
  • Other duties as assigned.

What you will need to be successful

Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s Degree, in information security, information technology, communications, marketing, education, instructional design, psychology, behavioral science, business, or related discipline is preferred. Equivalent experience in security awareness, human risk management, change management, communications, or enterprise program leadership may be considered.
  • 7+ years of professional experience in security awareness, human risk management, information security GRC, IT compliance, IT audit, privacy, legal, communications, marketing, education, instructional design, change management, or enterprise program leadership, preferably in a technology setting or highly regulated industry.

Specialized Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Proven experience leading enterprise security awareness, human risk management, or security culture programs in a regulated environment.
  • Strong ability to translate technical, regulatory, and risk concepts into clear business and teammate-facing communications.
  • Experience designing behavior-focused campaigns, executive communications, training programs, newsletters, videos, intranet content, and internal engagement strategies.
  • Strong creative direction skills, including the ability to turn complex security, fraud, privacy, compliance, and AI governance topics into memorable campaign themes, branded visuals, executive-ready materials, and teammate experiences that drive action.
  • Experience using phishing simulation data, training metrics, reporting trends, and engagement insights to measure program effectiveness.
  • Experience with O365 applications (Word, PowerPoint, Excel).
  • Additional Education/Certification preferred but not required, e.g. CIPP or CIPM, CDPSE, CISSP, CISM, CISA, CCSA.
  • Experience interacting with and working directly with/for internal/external business partners.
  • Able to work collaboratively in a fast-paced technology environment, where willingness to learn and adapt is critical.

jobs.description:
About the Department

The Operations Department manages DNDi’s corporate infrastructure globally across eight locations through its Business Development, Finance, Human Resources, Information Systems and Technology, Legal Affairs, and Project Management Office teams. The Department plays a central role in DNDi’s compliance and performance. 

Overview

The PMO Portfolio and Strategy Leader is a senior member of the PMO portfolio management team and works closely with the Head of the PMO to drive project management excellence across the organization. While the role can include working across all DNDi portfolios, the primary focus is on supporting the R&D portfolio and the incumbent will serve as the owner, within the PMO team, of the R&D portfolio. The role includes working with the R&D director, project teams, and senior management to support alignment of project selection with strategy, and take responsibility, along with Project leaders, for adequate and efficient planning and delivery, on time and on budget. The PMO Portfolio and Strategy Leader will also be responsible for managing, training, and mentoring other members of the team.

Responsibilities

Project Management Office (20%)

  • Work collaboratively with the Head of the PMO to update the PMO strategic plan, introduce initiatives, and promote program and project management excellence throughout the organization
  • Translate scientific opportunities into operational, feasible, and sustainable project plans (financial, resources, activities, risks, etc.)
  • Work closely with the R&D Director to ensure they remain informed of the status and progress of the projects as well as any issues that need to be escalated
  • Organize, with the R&D Director, the Scientific Internal Review Committee including agenda setting, follow-up, and minutes
  • Lead the R&D portfolio performance evaluation and tracking
  • Identify tools, trainings, and processes that will streamline and reinforce project management across the organization
  • Propose ideas/approaches to maintain and strengthen relationships between the PMO and other departments and functions, including external partners (where appropriate)
  • Manage a small team of PMO staff

Project and Portfolio Management (80%)

  • Developing strong relationships with the R&D Director, Cluster Directors, Heads of Disease, and disease teams
  • Drive project efficiency and adherence to timelines and budgets by supporting R&D leaders and project teams with project management processes and best practices
  • Proactively escalate critical project issues to the Cluster Director, Head of Disease, the Head of the PMO, and/or other leadership, as appropriate
  • Work with the disease teams, including through providing training and knowledge sharing, on tasks such as:
    • revising and refining the disease strategy
    • developing and updating project plans
    • identifying program/project risks and developing mitigation plans
    • defining project resources and allocation
    • coordinating with support functions such as procurement, business development, legal, etc.
    • ensuring compliance of the projects to all DNDi and funder/partner/stakeholder policies (where applicable) such as procurement, due diligence, contract management, etc.
    • other tasks as requested by the Head of Disease and/or disease teams and within the scope of the PMO
  • Serve as project manager for both R&D and non-R&D projects, as required

Additional /specific/projects responsibilities

  • Conduct all tasks in accordance with applicable DNDi Policies, Guidelines, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Working Instructions (WIs), and other Guidance and Standards

Reporting line & Interactions

  • The PMO Portfolio and Strategy Leader reports to the Head of the PMO
  • Works with other teams within the PMO and collaborates across the organization on both R&D and other portfolio projects, as needed.
  • Engages externally within defined projects, programs, teams, or functional areas, building and managing relationships with stakeholder groups relevant to their scope—such as partners, donors, vendors, or technical experts.
  • External engagement focuses primarily on operational and programmatic interactions that support project, program, or team objectives. Relationships are typically linked to specific initiatives or areas of responsibility rather than representing the organization at the broader institutional level

Experience and Education

  • A relevant post-graduate degree (biology, chemistry, medical sciences, etc.)
  • At least 10 years of progressively responsible experience in pharmaceutical development or a related industry
  • Proven track record in portfolio and project management and with delivering large, complex projects on time and on budget
  • Leadership or management training, including experience managing junior or mid-level team members
  • Experience launching new transformation initiatives or processes at an organization-wide level; solid experience with change management principles and implementation
  • Proven ability to work effectively in a culturally and geographically diverse team environment and matrix structure
  • Experience working in the public and private sector is a plus

Skills and competencies

Critical Skills

  • Advanced expertise and experience in managing complex and high-stakes projects and programs, in managing high-impact functions, .
  • Strong leadership in R&D program or functional development and delivery, with impact across teams, regions, or strategic areas.
  • Ability to provide expert advice and guidance to senior leaders on specialized topics within their domain.
  • Effective communication and ability to represent their area of responsibility in senior-level discussions.
  • Able to work autonomously and proactively to propose process improvement

Technical Skills

  • Experience managing R&D projects and programs through the entire lifecycle, beginning with initiating a proposal through project or program closure.
  • Demonstrated R&D Portfolio and Project management skills, including project planning, budgeting and monitoring and risk analysis
  • Good knowledge of clinical and pre-clinical development and regulatory requirements and processes with the ability to translate this into meaningful plans that can be used to set expectations and track project delivery.
  • Very strong ability to support the preparation of grant proposals, through coordination of the work and assembly of the different parts of the proposal, in particular the timelines and the budget.
  • Able to combine a strategic perspective, understanding the technical, regulatory and other objectives and constraints of disease areas and project teams, with a high level of focus on operational detail and the feasibility of project plans

Other requirements

  • Fluency in English
  • Proficiency in local languages desirable, especially French, Spanish and Portuguese
  • Excellent knowledge of Microsoft Suite

DEI Statement

DNDi is committed to building a diverse, equitable and truly inclusive organisation. Our success and global reach are dependent upon our ability to encourage diversity and draw on the skills, understanding and experience of all our people. We particularly welcome applications from those who are underrepresented in at DNDi and across the sector, especially women, and including, but not limited to, black and minority ethnic candidates, and those with other protected characteristic.

About Centric Software:

Centric Software® is a global leader, providing an innovative and AI-enabled product-concept-to-commercialization platform for retailers, brands and manufacturers of all sizes. We equip retail, fashion, luxury, footwear, outdoor, home and consumer goods brands with pioneering best-of-breed solutions to plan, design, develop, source, comply, buy, make, price, allocate, sell and replenish products. Our technology powers brands to streamline processes, drive efficiency and operate with confidence in an ever-changing market.

Our story is one of rapid growth, bold ideas and extraordinary opportunities. We’re here to challenge the status quo—and we’re looking for brilliant people who want to do the same. No matter where you are in the world, this is your chance to be part of something exceptional.

Job Title: Strategic Account Executive
Location: Remote, North America

Job Summary:

Centric Software is the global leader in Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) solutions, trusted by top names in fashion and retail. We are seeking an ambitious and experienced Strategic Account Executive to join our rapidly expanding global team and lead the sales efforts of our innovative solutions across North America.

As the Strategic Account Executive, you will be responsible for driving revenue growth by promoting Centric Software’s next-generation solutions to strategic leading retail and fashion brands. This is an exciting opportunity for a results-driven sales professional who is passionate about consumer products, fashion, technology, and business growth. You will play a key role in helping brands transform their product development processes, enhancing their time-to-market, and gaining a competitive edge.

By joining Centric Software, you will leverage our industry-leading PLM solutions to build long-lasting relationships with some of the most innovative fashion and retail brands in the world, providing them with the tools they need to optimize their product lifecycle from planning and design to delivery.

Responsibilities:

  • Own revenue generation within an assigned territory in North America

  • Build and maintain a qualified pipeline of sales opportunities.

  • Articulate the business value of all Centric Software’s solutions to stakeholders at all levels.

  • Lead complex sales cycles from opportunity identification to deal closure.

  • Analyze customer business needs and requirements to develop sales strategies and propose Product Intelligence Solutions.

  • Prepare and deliver written proposals, quotations, and responses to RFPs.

  • Strategize territory coverage to maximize reach and sales opportunities.

  • Deliver in-depth sales presentations on Centric PLM, Planning & Pricing solutions to retail and apparel companies.

  • Collaborate with technical teams to understand customer technology requirements; provide leadership for proposal and project teams.

  • Develop and manage a business plan for the assigned territory.

  • Represent Centric Software at regional and national trade shows, exhibits, and conferences.

Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of experience in enterprise sales, with a preference for net new business.

  • Proven track record of consistently meeting or exceeding annual quotas.

  • Experience in selling complex IT solutions to the retail sector is preferred.

  • Knowledge of PLM, Planning and product commercialization in retail or apparel

  • Excellent presentation skills at the executive level, both in small and large settings.

  • Proven ability to develop new business accounts.

  • Strong communication skills (both oral and written) and the ability to engage with multiple levels of decision-makers.

  • Experience preparing presentation materials and responding to RFPs.

  • Ability to build trust-based relationships with customers and cross-functional teams.

  • Adaptability to evolving technology and the commercial landscape.

  • Experience selling enterprise software solutions.

  • Familiarity with value-based or solution selling methodologies.

  • Knowledge of the MEDDIC sales process (Metrics, Economic Buyer, Decision Criteria, Decision Process, Identify Pain, Champion) and the ability to implement it effectively in sales strategies.

What We Offer:

  • Competitive salary and benefits package.

  • A high-responsibility, multifaceted role with significant opportunities for career growth.

  • A collaborative remote work environment built on flexibility, respect, and teamwork.

  • Challenging and varied work that will expand your business and technical skills.

Centric Software provides equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants without regard to race, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, color, age, religion, protected veteran or disability status or genetic information.

Job Title: Strategic Initiatives Support Officer

Cluster: Strategic Initiatives

Salary: USD 37,425.91 Per Annum, (Excluding Benefits)

Contract Type: 12 months (renewable), subject to satisfactory performance and funding availability

Location: Global - Remote (the successful candidate must have the right to work in the location where they are based)

Reports to: Advisor, Strategic Initiatives

Direct Reports: None

Role Overview:

The Strategic Initiatives Support Officer will provide high-quality project and administrative support to CIVICUS' Strategic Initiatives workstream, supporting activities to: strengthen funder engagement and grant management; diversify resource mobilisation efforts; support cross-cutting initiatives, including organisational strategy development, annual planning and budgeting, knowledge management, evaluations and learning, and support implementation of the Norad Civic Space grant. Working closely with the Advisor, Strategic Initiatives, the Officer will help ensure that funder reports, correspondence, briefing materials and knowledge products meet a consistently high editorial standard. Excellent writing skills and a high level of organisation are essential to this role.

Areas of Responsibilities & Key Activities

Writing, Research and Knowledge Products

  • Draft, edit and proofread funder correspondence, briefing notes, concept notes, talking points and other written materials to a high editorial standard, ensuring clarity, accuracy and consistency with CIVICUS' voice and style.
  • Support the development of content for concept notes and proposals, working with the Advisor, consultants and colleagues across CIVICUS on funding diversification efforts.
  • Prepare summaries, minutes and follow-up notes from meetings, forums and convenings.
  • Maintain and update knowledge resources and filing systems (e.g. Knowledge Hub/SharePoint), ensuring materials are accurate, current and easy to navigate.

Funder Engagement Support

  • Maintain and update funder contact records and CRM databases, ensuring information is accurate and current.
  • Support coordination with fundraising consultants, including scheduling calls, tracking agreed actions and consolidating outreach records.
  • Assist with preparation for funder meetings, forums and events, including logistics, briefing preparation and note-taking.
  • Support research into good funding practices and ecosystem-strengthening approaches for organisations and activists at risk.
  • Help track quarterly funder updates and other scheduled communications, flagging upcoming requirements to the Advisor.

Grant Management and Reporting (Accountability)

  • Maintain and update the Grants Management Profile (GMP) and Smartsheet dashboard, ensuring grant details, deliverables and reporting deadlines are accurate and current.
  • Schedule and support report coordination calls with project leads, Finance and I&A ahead of funder deadlines, tracking action points and following up on outstanding items.
  • Support quality-checking of narrative and financial reports for consistency, clarity and adherence to funder requirements.
  • Support documentation of grant agreements, restrictions and compliance requirements in collaboration with relevant teams.

Cross-Cutting Initiatives Support

  • Provide coordination and logistical support for annual planning, budgeting, learning activities, and other cross-organisational convenings, including scheduling, materials preparation and follow-up.
  • Support coordination of Norad-funded and other cross-organisational grant activities, liaising with cluster leads and coordinators to track progress.
  • Assist with organisational strategy review processes by compiling inputs, tracking action points and supporting follow-up.
  • Support project close-out processes (e.g. subgrant close-out, exit planning) by maintaining accurate records and tracking outstanding items.
  • Contribute to knowledge-sharing, knowledge management and learning initiatives by helping document, store, and disseminate lessons across teams and externally.

CIVICUS Values and Team Culture

  • Model CIVICUS' values and professional integrity in all written and verbal communications.
  • Contribute to a collaborative, supportive and high-performing team culture.

Other

  • This job description is not exhaustive, and the role holder will, from time to time, be required to carry out any other duties that are within the scope of the job and commensurate with the role, as reasonably assigned by management.
  • All staff will demonstrate CIVICUS values and principles in all their professional relationships and any interactions that may reflect on CIVICUS.

Person Specification

Education, Language & Qualifications

  • Minimum Bachelor's degree in social sciences, international relations, gender studies, sociology, political science, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience).
  • Excellent written and spoken English is essential; exceptional writing, editing and proofreading skills are a core requirement of this role.

Essential Knowledge, skills and Experience

  • Minimum 5 years' relevant work experience, ideally within a civil society organisation, international development or similar setting.
  • Demonstrated ability to write clearly, concisely and persuasively for varied audiences, including funders, policymakers and internal teams.
  • Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines with close attention to detail.
  • Good research and analytical skills, with the ability to synthesise information from a range of sources.
  • Commitment to human rights and social justice principles.
  • Experience working remotely and collaboratively within a globally distributed team.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office and project management applications.

Desirable Knowledge, skills and Experience

  • Experience supporting funder or grant reporting processes.
  • Knowledge of civil society and civic space issues.
  • Knowledge of one or more UN languages other than English.

The closing deadline for applications is on the 22 October 2026 at 11:59pm SAST.

Application instructions:

  • Applicants are advised not to use autofill when completing the application form for this job. To avoid errors, please fill out the form manually without using autofill.
  • AI-generated CVs/resumes and cover letters are not permitted. All application materials must be written by the applicant and accurately reflect the applicant’s skills, qualifications, and experience. Applications that contain AI-generated materials will not be considered.

Your application should comprise of:

  • A full CV, including educational and professional qualifications, a full employment history showing the positions, responsibilities held, and relevant achievements
  • A cover note of not more than one page outlining your motivation for applying for the role.

We appreciate and consider each application submitted. However, given the large volume of applications received, we find it impossible to respond to each applicant immediately. You will hear from us within three weeks only if you’re shortlisted for the next steps. We will update all applicants once the position has been filled.

CIVICUS reserves the right to withdraw any of our vacancies at any time.

  • Partner and field engagement
  • Execution against joint business plans and strategic initiatives

Take ownership.

Be accountable for your actions, your team, and the company. Accept responsibility willingly, especially when it’s what’s best for our customers. Give others every reason to trust you, believe in you, and count on you. Rise to every occasion with your personal best.

Be open.

Be open to new ideas. Be inclusive of people and ways of doing things. Make yourself accessible and approachable, and communicate with genuineness, transparency, honesty, and respect. Embrace differences.

Stay curious.

Stay curious even as you move forward. Tirelessly ask questions and challenge the status quo in your pursuit of new ideas, ways to solve problems, and to continually grow and improve.

Work as one.

Work together to create the best customer and workplace experience. Put our customers and employees first—before individual or departmental agendas. Make sure they get the help they need to succeed.

Equal opportunities

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Accurate will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws.

This posting is open for U.S.-based candidates who currently reside in the following states: AZ, CA, CO, DE, FL, GA, IL, KY, MD, MI, MN, NV, NH, NY, NC, OH, OK, PA, TN, TX, VA, WA, WV

jobs.description:
Position Summary
Inaccurate provider directory data is one of the most persistent and costly problems in U.S. healthcare. Members cannot reliably tell which clinicians are in network and accepting new patients, health plans carry real regulatory exposure under the No Surprises Act and CMS directory accuracy requirements, and providers are asked to verify the same information for dozens of payers. DataSpring sits at the center of that problem. Provider Directory is one of our highest-growth product lines, and we are investing to take it from a data asset to the market-leading directory solution for health plans.

We are seeking an experienced Principal Product Manager to own the success and evolution of DataSpring's Provider Directory product and domain. It pairs deep expertise in provider directory data and health plan directory operations with accountability for domain outcomes — from market and customer need through strategy, solution, funded delivery, commercialization, adoption, and performance. Provider Directory is the primary focus of this role, with secondary accountability for how Directory extends the broader Provider Data portfolio and our Universal Provider Data asset. This role will identify and evaluate new market and adjacent opportunities, ensure product strategy is aligned with industry mandates and regulatory considerations, and partner closely with UX, Technology, Data Science, and delivery teams to shape ideation, roadmap formation, and solution design, then steer delivery against committed outcomes — going deep into execution detail when a release, dependency, or escalation calls for it.

The Principal Product Manager owns the roadmap, the commercial model, and the KPIs that measure adoption, revenue, margin, and directory data quality. This is a multi-team influence role, setting direction across Technology, UX, Marketing, Sales, and Account Management and leading matrixed and contracted resources without direct reporting authority. The role engages health plan executives and buyers, provider organizations, and industry stakeholders, bringing fluency in buyer needs, procurement cycles, and directory operations, including network management, data intake, maintenance, outreach, and data verification, to improve how provider information is collected, governed, validated, and used across the healthcare ecosystem.

The Principal Product Manager is a full-time, remote, exempt position and reports to the Senior Director, Product Strategy and Management – Provider Data.

Specific Responsibilities

  • Own the success and evolution of the Provider Directory product and domain end to end, including growth of the existing Directory offering with health plans and its connection to the Universal Provider Data.
  • Identify and prioritize new market opportunities through customer discovery, competitive analysis, and business cases to guide investment decisions. Translate market needs, user personas, workflows, and data use cases into solution concepts, roadmap priorities, and product requirements.
  • Ensure strategy and roadmap reflect industry mandates, data governance expectations, directory accuracy and data quality standards, and interoperability requirements.
  • Validate concepts with advisory groups, customers, and industry stakeholders, including proofs of concept that inform commercialization and roadmap decisions.
  • Own the full product lifecycle for Provider Directory — strategy, concept, build, launch, growth, maturity, and retirement — setting the roadmap and funding case, and holding delivery teams to committed scope, timing, and outcomes while managing day-to-day execution when required. Serve as a subject‑matter expert and external advocate for Provider Directory, articulating strategic value to drive adoption and industry engagement.
  • Secure funding and resourcing for the roadmap through annual planning, weighing priorities against business objectives and customer need, and confirm work is ready for delivery teams.
  • Partner with Technology and UX to translate the business case into solution direction and requirements, and stay close enough to delivery to arbitrate tradeoffs and unblock decisions, working in the detail when a release demands it.
  • Monitor the competitive landscape and run market sizing and buyer analysis to identify differentiation and inform roadmap and go-to-market priorities.
  • Own packaging, and value proposition for Provider Directory offerings, with the business cases and ROI models behind them, to drive revenue growth, margin, and market expansion with health plans.
  • Influence go-to-market and commercialization for Provider Directory with Marketing, Sales, and Account Management — supporting positioning, value narratives, sales enablement, and reference use cases — and lead launch readiness across pilots, proofs of concept, and general availability.
  • Define, monitor, and report the KPIs tied to business cases and the annual plan, — adoption, revenue, margin, and directory data quality — and use them to guide ongoing investment.
  • Champion provider data accuracy, validation, and directory maintenance capabilities — source-of-truth reconciliation, continuous data quality monitoring, practitioner and primary source validation — as core differentiators of DataSpring's Directory solutions.

Skills

  • Strong strategic thinking and analytical skills, with the ability to lead market analysis, customer discovery, and competitive intelligence and translate complex market, business, and healthcare data insights into clear product strategy and investment recommendations.
  • Demonstrated experience managing provider directory data at scale, including data quality management; source-of-truth reconciliation across multiple contributing systems; provider verification of accuracy and primary source validation workflows; and identification, measurement, and remediation of directory data defects.
  • Expertise in developing compelling business cases, including financial modeling, ROI analysis, and growth potential assessment, to support prioritization and funding decisions.
  • Ability to define user personas, data use cases, and end-to-end solution concepts that connect customer problems to business outcomes.
  • Demonstrated capability to influence and align cross-functional stakeholders—including Product Management, UX, Technology, Data Science, Operations, Marketing, and external partners—without direct authority, in a high-growth, matrixed environment.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly articulate strategy, tradeoffs, and recommendations to executive, business, and technical audiences.
  • Comfort operating in ambiguity, balancing strategic vision with pragmatic constraints in a fast‑paced, evolving market environment.
  • Strong collaboration and relationship-building skills, including experience engaging customers, advisory groups, and industry stakeholders to validate strategy and inform product direction.
  • Proven ability to carry a roadmap through delivery — building the investment case that secures funding, framing scope, risk, and dependency tradeoffs, and holding teams to committed outcomes — with the technical fluency to engage in execution detail when needed.
  • Deep understanding of health plan buyer needs, procurement cycles, and provider directory operational workflows, including network management, provider data intake, directory maintenance, accuracy, and outreach.
  • Experience setting pricing, packaging, and positioning for data products and partnering with Marketing, Sales, and Account Management to drive adoption and expansion.

Experience & Education

  • 10+ years of product management, product strategy, data science, or healthcare data solutions experience, preferably within payer, provider, or health care information technology vendors.
  • Experience in supporting product development through engagement with a heavily vendor-driven development approach.
  • Working knowledge of the regulatory and compliance drivers behind provider directory accuracy — including No Surprises Act directory provisions, CMS Medicare Advantage and Medicaid directory accuracy requirements, and state network adequacy rules — and experience translating those requirements into data quality expectations and product decisions.
  • Domain experience in healthcare technology and data solutions, including privileging, data management, data governance, interoperability, and/or provider operations.
  • Experience developing and presenting strategic recommendations, business cases, and investment opportunities to executive leadership.
  • Familiarity with the provider directory and provider data vendor landscape.
  • Demonstrated success owning a product or domain end to end through a period of rapid growth, including launch and commercialization with health plan customers.
  • Experience managing network adequacy a plus.
  • Bachelor’s degree required.
  • Master’s degree preferred.
  • Degrees in healthcare administration, public health, or technology disciplines preferred.

Who We Are

DataSpring is the trusted data connector at the core of healthcare. For more than 25 years, we have powered the industry with the largest and most complete healthcare data foundation in the U.S., including more than 4.8 million provider data records sourced directly from providers and member data representing 75% of covered lives supplied by health plans. By improving how essential information flows across the system, DataSpring helps healthcare operate more efficiently, accurately, and with greater confidence.

What You Get

At DataSpring, you will do meaningful work at the intersection of healthcare, data, and technology, helping solve complex problems that make the healthcare system work better. You will collaborate with experienced professionals who care deeply about accuracy, trust, and meaningful impact in a fully remote environment.

DataSpring offers competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package for full-time employees, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) with company contributions and matching, paid parental leave, tuition assistance, and generous paid time off. We are committed to investing in our people and supporting professional growth over time.

Equal Opportunity Employer

DataSpring is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and is committed to fostering a workplace where all individuals are valued, respected, and empowered.

Employment decisions at DataSpring are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin or ancestry, age, marital status, disability, protected veteran status, personal appearance, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, familial status, family responsibilities, matriculation, political affiliation, genetic information, source of income, place of residence, or any other characteristic protected by law. jobs.title: Design Team Lead - Ecommerce Marketing Agency
jobs.excerpt: The Design Team Lead runs the day to day work of our Design Team.
jobs.description:
The Design Team Lead runs the day to day work of our Design Team. There are two sides to it. One is craft, which means keeping the standard of the design work high across every client we serve. The other is people, which means keeping the team organised, supported, and able to do good work without getting stuck.

Most of what the team produces is email and SMS campaign design for ecommerce brands, along with ad images, GIFs, short video edits, and the occasional landing page. You will still design yourself, but the larger part of the job is making sure what goes out is right. You are the person who spots what is not working in a design before the client does, and who explains the fix in a way a designer can act on straight away.

You will work closely with Account Managers, who assign the day to day tasks, and with the designers who carry them out. A good deal of the role sits between those two groups: helping an Account Manager work out what a campaign actually needs, turning that into clear direction for a designer, and saying so when a request does not make sense.

The Design Team Lead reports to the Service Director, and works closely with the other departments at Hustler Marketing to make sure design work is delivered well and on time.

About the Role:Mission statement:

To keep the quality of our design work at a level clients notice, and to run a team that is organised, well briefed, and heard.
The first half of that is craft. Reviewing work, spotting what is weak in a design, and giving direction that makes it better. The second half is people. Distributing the week, reorganising it when something changes, and making sure the team's ideas and concerns reach someone who can act on them. We already have a strong team here, independent and reliable. What they need from a lead is someone who listens properly and comes back with a real answer.


General Responsibilities:

Design quality and direction

  • Reviewing the team's design work before it reaches Account Managers or clients, and giving feedback specific enough to act on
  • Diagnosing why a design is not working, whether that is hierarchy, contrast, the weight of the call to action, the balance of image to text, or how it holds up on mobile, and writing the fix down clearly
  • Advising Account Managers on what a campaign needs visually, and pushing back when a brief is thin or a request will not serve the client
  • Designing directly when the workload calls for it. This is a hands-on role, not a purely supervisory one
  • Keeping the work consistent across a wide range of client brands, niches, and visual identities
  • Setting and holding the design standards for email and SMS campaigns, ad images, GIFs, and short video assets
  • Understanding each client's visual brand identity well enough to advise on ideas, improvements, and optimisations

Running the week

  • Distributing and organising the team's workload week by week, working from the tasks Account Managers assign
  • Reorganising the queue quickly when priorities change, someone is unavailable, or a client adds something at the last minute
  • Keeping track of who is overloaded and who is not, and rebalancing before it turns into a missed deadline
  • Being the first person the Design Team comes to when something is blocking their work
  • Making sure the design targets set for each client account are met

The team

  • Running the Design Team's group calls and regular one-to-ones
  • Collecting the team's suggestions and concerns, taking them seriously, and coming back with an answer, including when the answer is no
  • Mentoring designers and helping the less experienced members build their skills
  • Onboarding new designers into how we work
  • Connecting Design with the other service teams through workshops, short tutorials, and written documentation
  • Running training and skill-building sessions for the Design Team

Process and improvement

  • Noticing where a workflow, a handoff, or a piece of communication is costing the team time, and fixing it
  • Writing and maintaining the documentation the team works from
  • Keeping up with what Figma ships and bringing the useful parts into how the team works
  • Staying current on design and email marketing trends, and sharing what matters rather than everything
  • Bringing industry best practices back to the Service Director and to the team
  • Taking on projects and initiatives delegated by the Service Director


Position Specs:

  • Full-time commitment while meeting our general availability for office hours
  • An average of 140 tracked hours per month, consistently
  • Fixed-rate monthly salary paid in USD
  • Contractor status after signing our non-disclosure agreement
  • Exclusivity agreement, meaning you cannot hold a position of a similar nature elsewhere while working for Hustler Marketing
  • A 30-day notice period after the first month
  • Performance reviews every 9 to 12 months, with the first one after 3 to 6 months

Requirements

About you:

Profile:

You are a senior designer with at least five years behind you, and a portfolio of real client work across different brands and niches rather than a handful of personal projects. At least three of those years involve email marketing design.

You are expert in Figma. Not comfortable in it, expert. You should be able to build and maintain component libraries, and it helps if you follow what Figma releases closely enough to tell the team when something new is worth adopting. Adobe Creative Suite or Affinity is a useful complement, though we do not lean on either heavily.

You know more than one kind of design output. Email and SMS campaign design is the core of it, but ad images, GIFs, and short video edits come up constantly. Some basic knowledge of web design is a plus rather than a requirement, since landing pages appear from time to time and the team already handles most of that themselves.

What matters most is your eye, and how you talk about it. You can look at a design that is not performing and say what is wrong with it, in what order, and what you would change first. Then you can put that in a message a designer understands without needing a follow-up call. That skill is most of this job.

You are organised enough to run a week of work across several people, and to rearrange it at short notice without the whole thing falling apart.

You are the sort of person a team talks to. Ours is independent and reliable, and there are a few things they would like to see improved that are hard to change quickly. What matters to them is knowing their comments are being considered and answered, not that every one of them gets a yes.

You are curious. You notice when a process could be better and you do something about it instead of working around it. You bring people together across teams with workshops, documents, and tutorials without waiting to be asked.

And you notice detail, in your own work and in everyone else's.


Key traits for this position:

Strong visual judgement, and the vocabulary to explain it. Organised, and calm when the week changes shape. Approachable, and willing to have the honest conversation rather than the easy one. Curious about tools and trends without chasing every new thing. Detail-oriented past the point of comfort. At ease working remotely with people spread across several countries and time zones.


Key Requirements:

  • At least 5 years of experience as a graphic designer, with a minimum of 3 years in email marketing design
  • Expert-level Figma skills, including building and working from component libraries
  • Working knowledge of the Adobe Creative Suite or Affinity
  • Experience producing ad images, animated GIFs, and short video edits
  • An established portfolio showing on-brand, effective design work for a range of clients, stores, and niches
  • Experience leading, mentoring, or coordinating other designers. A formal lead title is not required, but you should have done the work
  • The ability to review someone else's design work and give written feedback that is specific and actionable
  • The ability to distribute and reorganise a team's weekly workload, including at short notice
  • A basic understanding of web design and landing pages is a plus
  • Experience with Klaviyo, or with a comparable email marketing platform, is a plus
  • Comfortable with Slack, Asana, Hubstaff, Google Workspace, and Figma, and willing to learn whatever else we use
  • Fluent written and spoken English. It does not need to be your first language, but you will be writing feedback and running calls in it every day
  • Remote work experience, ideally with a team spread across time zones
  • Available and responsive during office hours, Monday to Friday between 3 and 6 PM Barcelona time
  • Consistently working 30 to 35 hours per week, which is 140 hours per month
  • A stable internet connection, a laptop or PC, and the ability to join video calls

We're looking for an AI Engineer to contribute to the development and delivery of AI/ML systems. This role is ideal for an early-career engineer who is comfortable writing code, eager to take on real responsibility, and ready to grow their craft.

In this role, you will work as a contributing member of a cross-functional team, building and supporting AI/ML models, pipelines, and the systems around them. You'll take ownership of well-scoped tasks, learn from more senior engineers, and steadily expand the surface area you can confidently deliver on. You'll be joining real, in-flight work where reliability and quality matter. You'll collaborate closely with experienced engineers to build new capabilities, improve existing systems, and develop the technical instincts that come from shipping things that matter.

Why This Role Matters

At Robots & Pencils, we design AI systems for a human world. Our name says it all. Robots and pencils means engineering paired with creativity, because every agent we ship has to work for real people in real workflows. That balance is baked into how we operate.

Every role here contributes directly to that mission. Here, you shape how AI systems integrate into enterprise operations, how teams move at real velocity, and how products create measurable impact for clients and the people they serve. We ship production-ready AI in 30 to 45 days. That pace demands people who take ownership, lead with craft, and care deeply about what they put their name on.

What You’ll Do

Craft & Delivery

  • Build and ship features of AI/ML and LLM-powered systems with guidance from senior engineers, contributing to solutions that run in production
  • Implement and maintain components of AI/ML and AI agent pipelines from data ingestion through model deployment, picking up the unglamorous parts as you grow
  • Contribute to LLM-powered features such as prompts, evaluations, retrieval, and tool integrations, working alongside senior engineers
  • Handle data preprocessing, feature engineering, and basic evaluation to prepare quality inputs and validate model and prompt performance

Collaboration & Communication

  • Work closely with engineers across a distributed, cross-functional team to move projects forward effectively
  • Document experiments, results, and model decisions clearly so findings can be built upon, replicated, and shared across the team
  • Participate in code reviews and team discussions, contributing your perspective and incorporating feedback

Leadership & Influence

  • Take ownership of assigned tasks and deliver end-to-end with consistency and follow-through
  • Share learnings from experiments and research with the broader team, contributing to a culture of continuous improvement
  • Bring intellectual curiosity to every problem — ask good questions, explore new approaches, and stay hungry to grow your craft

What You’ll Bring

  • 3+ years of professional software engineering experience, with hands-on exposure to AI/ML systems and generative AI development
  • Solid software engineering foundation (Python or similar)
  • Foundational knowledge of cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure), with interest in deepening AWS and AWS GenAI expertise
  • Exposure to building or contributing to agentic AI systems alongside more senior engineers
  • Familiarity with AI frameworks and orchestration tools
  • Familiarity with evaluation and observability practices for LLM apps
  • Awareness of AI safety, responsible AI principles, prompt injection risks, and PII handling
  • Exposure to RAG pipelines: chunking strategies, embedding models, and vector databases
  • Experience building or integrating with APIs, including internal and third-party services
  • Awareness of LLM cost considerations such as token economics and caching strategies
  • Working knowledge of Docker for containerized deployments, with exposure to Kubernetes
  • Demonstrable, day-to-day usage of AI-forward coding tools such as Claude Code and Cursor

Helpful Extras and Unique Skills

You’ll Do Well Here if You Are

  • A doer. You see something broken and fix it. You'd rather move on clarity than wait for certainty.
  • A fast learner who knows you don't know everything. The AI landscape changes weekly. You're senior enough to know better and curious enough to keep learning anyway.
  • Direct in a way that makes the work better. You give honest feedback. You'd rather have the hard conversation than blow smoke.
  • Obsessed with craft. You know genius is in the details. You ship exceptional, not perfect, and you don't put your name on work you wouldn't stand behind.
  • Built for ownership. You honor commitments, admit mistakes fast, and back your teammates when a decision costs something. No handoffs, no finger-pointing.
  • All in. You treat clients' businesses like your own. You take the work seriously without taking yourself seriously.
  • Resourceful when the budget, timeline, or team is tight. Constraints don't slow you down. They sharpen you.
  • Glad to be in the room with people who care as much as you do. Our teams average fifteen-plus years of experience. We hire people who push each other to do better work.

The ESM team also maintains configuration data for all customer applications and devices deployed to on-premises and cloud environments in a Configuration Management Database (CMDB).

The ESM team participates in all Priority 1 and select Priority 2 incident bridge calls and supports the development and submission of Root Cause Analysis (RCA) documentation for review and approval by the customer.

The team also hosts the Daily Operations Review Meeting (DORM) with customer operational support teams, reporting on Priority 1 incident outage activity and any other significant incidents or changes impacting services.

What you will do:

  • Identify, document, and manage configuration items (CIs) needed to deliver IT services, including their relationships and dependencies:
